Draft 
 
August 9th Prudential Committee Monthly Minutes 
Members Present - Mel Biggs, Jonathan Vincent, Bob Chamberlin, Cheryl Lindberg (treasurer) Brion 
McMullan (Administrator)  
Guest - David Hubbard (Land Management Council), Priscilla Vincent (District Elected Auditor) 
 
Meeting called to order at 5:30pm in small conference room, Tracy Hall 
Reports -  
Clerk ‘s report - Minutes of June 14th were reviewed and approved as presented. 
 
Treasurer's report - report of Water Department "Certificate of Deposit" bids, highest was Mascoma 
Savings at .85%. Committee approved Cheryl accepting Mascoma's offering.  
Cheryl presented a sheet calculating the revenue to be raised from the finalized Town Grand List 
through the Fire District tax. She proposed a rate of 0.0510. This is .0002 over last year's rate. Brion, 
District Administrator, objected to the minor increase. He believed the Annual report had proposed no 
increase and the information presented to attorneys and homeowners since the beginning of the 
calendar year had reflected this position. Committee approved Cheryl's proposed rate to better reflect 
the amount listed in the budgeted financials. 
June warrants were reviewed by Committee members and signed,  paper copies of June's financials 
were not available so Cheryl gave a verbal report.   
 
Committee chose to step out of order and address the next issue in deference to their guest . 
 
Walsh's timber trespass - Dave Hubbard, Land Management Council, reported on his visit to Parcel #2 
abutting the Walsh's property and the feelings of the Land Management Council.  Jonathan spoke and 
Bob supported the importance of a letter to the Walshs of the Committee concern regarding the 
removal of trees and flagging a trail without first consulting with either the Land Management Council or 
the Prudential Committee.  A decision was made to consult with Harwood Forestry, forestry 
management for the Land Management Council, regarding the value of the trees cut. Jonathan to draft a 
letter to the Walshs to explain the Committee is still collecting information and the importance of their 
not cutting  trees or brush as well as  trail work on District property without obtaining permission.  Dave 
Hubbard then went on to update the Committee on Land Management Council trail improvements 
through the VYCC and an Eagle Scout project to remove trash along the bank by the parking area at the 
top of the Ballard Trail. 
 
Administrator's  Report for July and August - Responsible Party - Sam Eaton to be listed with Water 
Supply as a responsible party allowing him to sign monthly reports ( Committee approved), Farrell 
Gravel Pit Access Easement - Brion reported on Stuart Close's (Twin State Sand & Gravel) estimate of 
time and equipment needed to partially reclaim the District's portion of the pit. Brion proposed the 
District consider authorizing an access easement for five years. Committee requested more information 
on the value of the material in the pit. Watershed Land Survey - Bill Lyons, surveyor, requested direction 
on calculating acreage defined by Town roads "Right of Way" or total acreage surveyed. Committee 
approved calculating defined by R.O.W..  Carpenter Street Swale - Senior Housing is working with Pete 
Moseley on regarding their swale. Their swale drains into the Carpenter Street swale and has created 
some sediment issues in the past and currently. Brion asked if the Committee wished to be a party in 
discussion with anticipated regarding to address issues in our section. Jonathan reminded the 

Committee they had voted to no longer maintain the swale other than to continue cutting the grass 
after Dana Young from Soil Conservation in 2000 determined the project had reached the end of its 
useful life. Jonathan remembered the Committee approached the neighborhood and the Town to pass 
over the easements granting authority to maintain the swale and no takers were forth coming. Brion 
suggested that as we still held the easements some responsibility or liability may still exist to the 
District. He suggested the Committee have our attorney review. Committee declined at this time. Bob 
wondered if there was a time limit to the easements. Brion did not think so. Brion is to provide a sample 
copy of the access and maintenance easements to Bob.  
 
 
General Business -  
Deborah Dufty letter - Deborah is concerned on legality of District penalty policy regarding delinquent 
accounts . Committee reviewed Deborah's letter and Title 24, Chpt. 129 Uniform Water and Sewer 
Disconnect from the Vermont State Statutes. Brion reported on his inquiries with the Secretary of 
State's Office and VLCT Law review and neighboring municipalities.  Committee requested Jonathan 
write Deborah to let her know they had reviewed her letter and would be collecting more information 
regarding their policy before addressing her concerns.  
 
Appeals - Janice Lavoie and Kate Riley - high water usage due to unanticipated leaks - Committee 
approved forgiveness half above average usage per their unanticipated leak policy. 
 
Due to the time all other business was postponed till a later meeting. 
 
Next meeting scheduled for September 20th. 
 
Call to adjourn at 7:50pm.

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT      DRAFT           
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
      September 20, 2010 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Mel Biggs, Bob Chamberlin, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg 
Anne French, 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:34 in the small conference room in Tracy Hall, Norwich, 
VT. 
 
The minutes of the August 9th meeting were approved as presented with one correction. The 
final sentence of the Treasurer's Report will now read "May and June warrants were reviewed 
by Committee members and signed, paper copies of the June's financials were handed out;  
Cheryl gave a verbal report." 
 
Mel Biggs will not be running for re-election as a member of the Prudential Committee at the 
2010 annual meeting.  Bob Chamberlin will be retiring at the same time with one year 
remaining in his term. The District list will be distributed to the Prudential Committee to help 
discover potential candidates. 
 
 August financials for the Fire District Fund, the Water Fund, and the Reserve Funds were 
handed out and reviewed. Sidewalks will need to be adjusted on the asset list. Payables and 
payroll warrants for August were signed. 
 
The Committee authorized Brion to contact Provan and Lorber to tell them we want 
closure on the BOD. We will let them decide how to wrap it up. The Committee agreed that 
the BOD is a useful research document, even in draft form.  However, since it was written as a 
funding document, there are items in it that we won't be pursuing. Brion sent Provan and 
Lorber his list of suggested changes in March. Although they reviewed that list, we have had no 
response from them since early June. We had been billed for the whole BOD, but paid them 
only half since the document is still incomplete. 
 
The Committee voted unanimously to buy 50 - 100 used T-10 meter heads. We now have 
50 new T-10s in stock and there are 40-50 T-10s in the system. Brion will also buy used outside 
readers so we can stay with our present system for a few more years. Eventually we'll have to 
switch over but by then the cost of meters and reading guns will have come down. Presently, 
salary and postage cost $1,800 to have Sam and Brion process the quarterly reading an average 
of  $38,000. 
 
Brion was authorized to draft a written agreement with the Farrells. This will outline the 
terms of remediation and mitigation for the access to the gravel pit that runs across our land . 
The  Farrells are not regulated by Act 250 because they are taking out less than the 

grandfathered 37,000 cubic yards a year.  The Committee will want terms of remediation to be 
in writing.  At the next meeting the Committee will whether to charge a toll for use of our 
access based on materials extracted.  
 
Jonathan will write a letter to the Walshes about their timber trespass on Parcel #2. Our 
forester stated in his letter that the trees are valued at $193. The Walshes will owe the Land 
Management Committee for the trees as well as $112.50 for our forester's fee. Jonathan's letter 
will also say that the LMC needs to be contacted about the trail. The letter might say also that 
punitive damages could be considered should there be another trespass.  
 
The LMC will need to circulate a petition and get at least 40 signatures in order to continue the 
tax exemption for the Watershed Lands.  Jonathan will write Dave Hubbard, reminding him 
this must be done by late January. 
 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on Monday, October 25, at 5:30 pm in the small 
conference room in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT.  This will be the first budget meeting. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:09 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT             
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
      October 26, 2010 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Mel Biggs, Bob Chamberlin, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg, 
Anne French, and visitors Priscilla Vincent, Ruth Jabs, Ted Jabs 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:30 pm in the small conference room in Tracy Hall, 
Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the September 20th meeting were accepted as amended. The first sentence now 
reads "5:34 pm" and the last sentence in the Farrell paragraph states that the "Committee will 
discuss whether …". 
 
 Written copies of the financial reports through September 30th were handed out and reviewed. 
The September warrants were signed. Citizen's Bank will be leaving Norwich so Cheryl has 
asked Ledyard and Mascoma Banks to tell us what banking services they could offer us. The 
Committee will choose a new bank after hearing from these two. The renewal of our annual 
insurance policy with VLCT was reviewed and approved. By unanimous vote of the 
Committee Mr. Ratliff's penalty was waived.  Bob will set up a spread sheet for the 
November budget meeting, and, using his projector, the Committee will enter in the anticipated 
year end amounts and known increases. 
 
Kate Chamberlin will be asked to head up the Nominating Committee for the Annual Meeting 
again this year. 
 
The draft survey of Parcel #1 was reviewed and accepted with one amendment. William 
Lyons will be asked to label Paul Donahue's parcel off Kate Wallace Road. After making this 
change, Mr. Lyons will record the survey with the Town. We will ask him to give us estimates 
for surveying Lots # 2 and #4. We will ask other surveyors for estimates and we might delay 
making a decision for a year.  
 
The Committee voted to have Brion draft a letter to the Farrells to open negotiations 
about their gravel pit access easement.  The Committee wants, in writing, the terms of the 
proposed remediation, a time limit for the access easement, and a statement whether the access 
fee will be based on a per yard or percentage basis. Additional costs would also need to be 
negotiated. There are approximately 100,000 cubic yards of material, worth $500,000, left in 
the pit. Only 37,000 cubic yards can be removed annually.  Remediation has been estimated to 
cost about $7,000 and will take about a week. Tree cutting would be carried out by a forester in 
exchange for the lumber and the final grade of the slope on our land would be 10%, maximum. 
 
The letter to Mr. and Mrs. Walsh was approved with the following changes. In the second 
paragraph Land Management Committee will be changed to Land Management Council in two 
places. The second sentence of the third paragraph will read "…  the Land Management 
Council, which is ….". A time frame for payment of the penalty will be included. 

 
The letter to Mrs. Duffy about late payment notifications was approved with the addition of 
two moderating words. 
 
Provan and Lorber's Andy Sharpe would like to go over the BOD, which he refers to as a 
Preliminary Engineering Report. He says they have already spent more money on this than they 
will ever be paid. When the BOD was initiated it was to be a funding document for one big 
project covering a variety of issues. However, it would now only be useful to us if becomes a 
prioritized list of projects to be accomplished incrementally. The Committee reviewed Brion's 
bulleted list of priorities and comments. We will give them our list, ask if they agree, and ask 
them to put the list in the revised "recommended plan" along with cost information for the 
projects. We are eager to wrap this up. 
 
The Committee reviewed the Administrator's Report and had a lengthy discussion about ways 
to improve the functioning of the Fire District's office. 
 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on Monday, November 15, at 5:30 pm in the 
small conference room in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT.  
 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:45 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT        DRAFT        
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
November 15, 2010 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Mel Biggs, Bob Chamberlin, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg, 
Anne French, and visitors: Priscilla Vincent, Vince Watts, Barbara Currier, Andy Hodgdon 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:35 pm in the small conference room in Tracy Hall, 
Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the October 26th meeting were accepted as amended. The middle sentence of the 
third paragraph will now read "By unanimous vote of the Committee, the penalty and interest 
on Mr. Ratliff's tax bill were waived." 
 
The October warrants were reviewed and signed. After a discussion, comparing the two 
Norwich banks, the Committee voted unanimously to select the Mascoma Bank to become 
the Fire District's bank as it offered us more advantages. Our former bank, Citizens Bank, is 
closing its Norwich office.  
 
The Administrator's report was reviewed. Brion will call Dorann Farrell to confirm her receipt 
of his letter concerning the access easement to the gravel pit and will ask her to make us a 
proposal before the December meeting. The Prudential Committee will discuss this proposal 
with her at that meeting. The rate and time period need to be decided. Revised estimates show 
that there are 370,000 cu.yds, not 100,000 cu. yds., of sand left in the pit. This means the pit can 
operate for another ten years. A formal, written legal document must be drawn up by December 
31, 2010. Should there be no easement in force by January 1, 2011 we would have the right to 
deny access to the gravel pit across Fire District land. 
 
Paper copies of the proposed 2011 budget, incorporating the October financials, were handed 
out. The hiring of an office assistant/bookkeeper was discussed. This would not increase our 
expenses since Brion will be decreasing his time by eight hours. The office assistant would have 
a twelve hour week with no benefits. The wages would be allocated in a 60/40 split between the 
Water Department and the Fire District and would be capped at $9,500 a year. 
 
Andy Hodgdon presented his proposal for a Main Street drainage project from the intersection 
with Beaver Meadow Road to the north entrance of Hazen Street. This would include new 
granite curbing for this section of the sidewalk. Should the Prudential Committee approve 
contributing $21,000 for curbing to this joint effort with the Town, the Town would then take 
ownership of that sidewalk. We could finance this expense from the $85,000 we still have left 
in our bond and budget it all to this year.  We could borrow from the Water Fund and budget it 
over two years, treating it as a capital expense, paying the $21,000 back with 4% interest. We 
will know by Town Meeting if the drainage project will proceed. This would give us time to 
prepare for replacing the existing 1922 pipe under Main Street between Trumbull Lane and the 
Jabs house, We already have the design for this work and have been talking about this sidewalk 

since the early 1990's. Andy hopes to start work in July.  It appears that the Town is willing to 
take over our remaining half mile of sidewalks but only after we have improved them. The 
Prudential Committee will consider talking to the Town Manager and the Select Board about 
the sidewalks. Due to these possible expenses next summer, the Committee agreed to postpone 
the surveying of another Watershed parcel.  
 
The Committee feels that funds raised by the Land Management Council's forestry activities 
should be used for the surveys of our watershed lands.  
 
Job evaluations were reviewed by the Committee. Discussions about COLA, dental insurance, 
health insurance, and job descriptions will be held at the next meeting of the Prudential 
Committee.  
 
The Annual Meeting of the Fire District will be held on January 24th, 2011. The next Prudential 
Committee meeting will be held on Tuesday, December 14th, at 5:30 pm in the small conference  
room in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT.  
 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:35 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT           DRAFT   
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
December 15, 2010 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Mel Biggs, Bob Chamberlin, Sam Eaton, Cheryl Lindberg, 
Anne French, and visitors: Dorann Farrell, Priscilla Vincent, Vince Watts, Barbara Currier 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:40 pm in the small conference room in Tracy 
Hall, Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the October 26th meeting were accepted presented. 
 
The November warrants were reviewed and signed.  
 
Cheryl will be hiring a bookkeeper. Doug Wexford said he is willing to serve as 
assistant treasurer. The Committee voted unanimously to authorize Doug to 
sign checks. Six households still owe Fire District taxes ($36.00 -$250.00). They 
were all sent reminder notices in October, November, and December and received 
a phone call last week about the delinquent taxes. 
 
Sam and Bob report that all is going well while Brion is sailing in Antarctica. The 
overflow pipe at the reservoir has been fixed. Customers have complained recently 
about glasses not being well cleaned by dishwashers. This smudging is caused by 
the newly formulated dishwasher soaps, required to be phosphate-free, not by our 
fine water. 
 
The Farrell gravel pit still contains an estimated 300,000 cubic yards of bank run 
fill. As this is unscreened and can't be used for road sand, there isn't much demand 
for the material and it might take as long as 25 years to close the pit. We would 
like to have the remediation done on our part of the pit now for safety and stability 
of the site.  There is money in the escrow account available for this. The 
Committee will propose a per cubic yard fee for continuing the access easement 
across Fire District property for the next 25 years. This proposal will be presented 
to the Farrell family by year's end. 
 
The Committee held a lengthy discussion about the 2011 budget. As it is the 
Committee's goal to get out of the sidewalk business, we will pay for a normal 
repair to the Beaver Meadow sidewalk and let the Highway Department make up 
the difference. After the repair is completed we will turn over that section of 
sidewalk to the Town. Last year we spent $20,000 for sidewalk repair. We should 
be able to turn over our remaining sidewalks to the Town within 3 years. It will 
cost us $30,000 to make the necessary repairs before the transfer. Hopefully we 
can use $11,000 from our bond fund for these repairs.  
 

We now have $165,000 sitting in reserve for emergencies. This could be reduced 
to $120,000 but we must have adequate funds ready to move fast whenever the 
Town decides to go ahead with its Main Street project. A very serious break would 
cost us $15,000 -$30,000 to repair but a cave-in of the reservoir roof would cost 
much more. The tax and water rates will remain the same for 2011. 
 
At 7:35 pm the Prudential Committee went into executive session to discuss terms of the 
new agreement with Farrell Associates for the gravel pit easement.  
 
At (?) pm the Committee came out of executive session.  While in executive session the 
Committee decided to authorize Brion to talk with Farrell Associates to resolve three 
issues: establishment of a fee based on a percentage of the price per cubic yard, a set time 
limit for the new easement, and the commencement of the remediation of our land sooner 
rather than later.  
 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on Monday, January 17th, 
at 5:30 pm in the small conference room in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT. The Annual 
Meeting of the Fire District will be held on Monday, January 24th, 2011 to be 
followed by the Prudential Committee's regular January meeting. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT           DRAFT    
        PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
March 7, 2011 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg, 
Anne French, and auditor Priscilla Vincent 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:31 pm in the in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the January 24th meeting were accepted as presented. The minutes 
of the 2011 Annual Meeting were reviewed. 
 
The Committee voted unanimously to require 2 signatures for checks over 
$3,000. The Treasurer and a member of the Prudential Committee will be the 
signers. This will ensure that both signers will be familiar with the background of 
the expense. All three Committee members will be on the bank's signature cards. 
Checks of this amount are only cut 4-6 times annually.  
 
On March 1st a leak of 70,000 gpd (50 gpm) was located at the intersection of 
Route 10 and I-91's southbound ramp. This is the second time this line has broken 
since this half mile of pipe was laid by the State in 1968.  The pipe is made of 
ductile iron so it should not have broken. Ductile iron should not develop 
circumfrential cracks but this pipe has them because, unfortunately, the State 
decided to add 10' of fill over the pipe which was laid into hardpan clay with fill 
around it.  Now the gravel is settling and the pipe is breaking. L&M responded 
quickly but repairs were complicated since the pipe was 10' deep, the wiring for 
the traffic signals' pressure sensitive plates had been mislocated during the 
Corridor Enhancement work, and there were several conduits near the break. We 
had very good cooperation with Hanover setting up connection plans for Lewiston 
and McKenna Road. Fortunately the plans did not need to be implemented since 
water service to those areas was only stopped from Thursday morning until midday 
Friday. The Water Department received compliments from the 30 affected 
residents and the State paid for traffic control. 
 
For the past 6 weeks we have been using the test well while awaiting the 
installation of our new autotransformer on well #2. This proves the value of 
keeping the old well functioning.  
 
Jamie Hess would like to use the old Gospel Church property, in the Adaptive 
Reuse Zone north of the pump house, for a bike shop and residence. We will 
review his plans to be sure there will be no impact on our wells. 
 
We still have no closure with Provan and Lorber for the BOD. 
 
We have received 125 responses from our 325 customers for e-mail addresses. 
 

Brion's report on the Farrell Gravel Pit Access Easement was reviewed and 
discussed. The Committee voted unanimously to have Norwich Associates pay 
us $7,500 now out of escrow for remediation, to set up a 5 year easement that 
may be renewed 3 additional times, to have Jack Candon draw up an 
agreement for us to sign, and to authorize Stu Close to do $7,000 worth of 
remediation.  
 
By unanimous vote the Committee authorized Jay Van Arman's starting 
salary, as Part-time Weekend Operator, to be $15.00 an hour. 
 
The Treasurer handed out paper copies of the year-to-date financials. The January 
and February warrants were reviewed and signed. The changeover from Citizen's 
Bank to Mascoma Bank is 99.5% completed. 
 
Cheryl will be talking to the Town's Assistant Bookkeeper, who also does work 
for the Listers' Office, about working part time for the Fire District on Wednesday 
and Friday afternoons. She uses the same software for the Town that we use.  
 
The Committee accepted and signed the Forestry Contract for work at the gravel 
pit. The forester will get 20% of the gross. The cost of the cutting will be covered 
by the timber sale even though wood prices are down. 
 
The Long Range Planning Meeting will be held on April 27, 2011 at the Norwich 
Inn beginning at 8:00 am with a field trip to the pump house and gravel pit. 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on Wednesday, April 27, 
2011 in the Norwich Inn, following the Long Range Planning Meeting.  
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:10 pm. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT                  DRAFT 
        PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
   April 27, 2011 
 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg, 
Anne French, and guest Dave Hubbard 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:31 pm in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the March 24th meeting were accepted with this change in the first 
sentence of the third paragraph: "test well" was changed to "well #1". 
 
Dave Hubbard, Chairman of the Land Management Council, reported that Paul Harwood 
of Tunbridge is the new forester for the LMC. The Council is planning to do commercial 
thinning, taking out lowgrade timber this winter, from the 100 acres behind the log 
landing. The Prudential Committee's responsibility is only to approve the contract, not to 
make decisions about management. By unanimous vote the Committee authorized the 
LMC to engage Harwood Forestry to mark trees, to look for interested loggers, and 
to return to the Prudential Committee with their recommendation.  The Committee 
received Susan McCoy's letter of resignation from the LMC and appointed Sandy 
Haskell, a resident of the Fire District, to replace her. Chairman Vincent will write Susan 
a letter of appreciation for her 13 years of loyal and enthusiastic work with the Council.  
 
The LMC has applied to the Vermont Youth Conservation Council for a grant to improve 
the trail from our old dam to the Town pool. The Prudential Committee voted 
unanimously to use the money for this purpose. Dave Hubbard said there is interest in 
developing a mountain bike trail along Beaver Meadow Road on Parcels 4 and 6, from 
the Brown Schoolhouse bridge to the parking lot at the top of the hill. Before giving Dave 
permission to do a feasibility study of the proposed project, the Committee wants to walk 
the site.  VLCT would also have to review the project for liability issues. 
 
The Walsh paid their timber trespass penalty and the Harwood Forestry fee in December. 
 
A full set of written financial statements was handed out and reviewed by the Committee. 
The March warrants were reviewed and signed. 
 
The Prudential Committee voted unanimously to give Ben Tilden an extra $750 for 
installing the 60hp VFD, if Provan & Lorber's design review costs less than the $12,500 
estimated maximum. The Committee voted unanimously to replace and improve  the 
broken pipe on Koch Road with 1.5" copper pipe. 
 
 

 
The Committee reviewed their copies of Provan & Lorber's Basis of Design. The BOD 
states the monitoring equipment in the pump house needs to be upgraded in order to 
comply with groundwater rule log 4. This capital improvement will cost us $27,400 plus 
the design cost. Brion will look into finding us a new engineering firm that specializes in 
pump houses to help us with this upgrade. 
 
Andy Hodgdon will attend the May meeting to discuss the repaving of Main Street from 
Beaver Meadow Road to Route 5. The Committee voted unanimously to support 
Brion's negotiating with the Town to finalize ownership of the District's sidewalks. 
 
Bill Lyons has asked us if we want to proceed with surveys of Parcels # 2 and #3. 
 
Brion was authorized to hire the robot to clean our reservoir for $900. Payment will  
be made in 2012. To have the cleaning done by manually would have cost $3,000.  
 
Brion said we can pay for the recent water main breaks with  $20,000 out of our 
operating funds but will have to replace the money eventually. Cheryl will look at Dave 
Datillo's notes from our 1998 regarding use of our capital funds. 
 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on May 16, 2011 in the small 
conference room in Tracy Hall at 5:30pm. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 3:25pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT                       DRAFT             
        PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
   May 16, 2011 
 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Anne French, and guest 
Ben Smith 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:40pm. 
 
The minutes were accepted with changes to two sentences. They now read: "The meeting was 
called to order at 1:10pm in the Norwich Inn."  "The Walshes paid their timber trespass 
penalty…" 
 
The Committee met with Ben Smith, whose backyard was damaged by the May 9th water main 
break on McKenna Road following the fire department drill.   The Fire District has spent $500 
to fill the hole in the Zeiglers', (his neighbors') driveway. Ben is considering his options and 
will be talking with the Town and Fire District about this situation. Ben said he was impressed 
at how promptly Brion and Sam responded to the emergency. 
 
Brion suggested that the Prudential Committee pay part of Sam's medical insurance out of the 
unspent funds budgeted for our office staff. 
 
The Committee reviewed the draft of our Ten Year Plan and made one change. No second gate 
will be installed at the gravel pit. The Committee then adopted the Plan by unanimous vote. 
 
Dave Webb's appeal was granted by forgiving half the overage for the last quarter.  
The Committee also voted unanimously to forgive Dr. Pinello's catch up billing, which was 
due to the faulty reader and the honest misunderstanding regarding the policy relating to the 
former owner. Jonathan will draft a letter to her laying out the situation and send it to the 
Committee for its review. 
 
Three engineering firms, Vision, Otter Creek, and Elliott and Anderson, have expressed an  
interest in working with us on the pump house upgrade. Brion will send them copies of Provan 
and Lorber's BOD and, after selecting a firm, hopes to start work this summer 
 
The Committee reviewed the Andy Hodgdon's draft proposal for accepting the Fire District's 
remaining sidewalks. Andy says the Town will only accept our sidewalks if they are in good 
order. Over the past 5 years we have spent $70,000 - $80,000 on sidewalks. According to 
Andy's estimates, we will need to spend $15,000 annually for the next 5 years ($75,000) to 
bring our sidewalks up to Town standards.  The District has been using macadam curbing while 
Andy wants granite curbing which costs 5 or 6 times more. To repair just the Huntley Meadow 
sidewalk to Town standards would cost the District $40,000.  By unanimous vote the  
 
 

 
Prudential Committee agreed not to make any final decisions about our sidewalks, nor to 
commit any funds, until after the Committee meets with the Select Board this summer. 
Brion will advise the Town Manager and Andy of this vote and make arrangements for a 
meeting. After a decision is made, the issue will have to go before the District at our Annual 
Meeting in January. 
 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on June 20th, 2011 in the small conference 
room in Tracy Hall at 5:30pm. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 8:00pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT              DRAFT                        
        PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
     July 25, 2011 
 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg, 
Anne French, and guests Roger Blake, Ed Childs, Pete Webster, Andy Hodgdon, and Priscilla 
Vincent 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:36 pm in the Multi-Purpose Room in Tracy Hall, 
Norwich,VT. 
 
The minutes from the June meeting were accepted as presented with one change.  In the 
second to last sentence of the last paragraph, Treasurer Lindberg's title was changed from 
"Co-Administrator" to  "Company Administrator." 
 
Andy Hodgdon's proposal for the Transfer of Sidewalk Ownership was reviewed by 
everybody. All were in agreement that Public Works and the Fire District should make 
every possible effort to coordinate pipe replacement and road projects so as to avoid 
ripping up the pavement twice. Andy agreed that we should replace the 1922 mains and 
old valves at the Hazen/Main intersection this fall. We'll do a small amount of patching 
the road after and he'll do his drainage work and repaving next year. We have bids out 
now for our work.  
 
Several points of concern were raised about the sidewalks. The Town's road work 
impacts the sidewalks, not vice versa. While the District no longer is able to put $15,000-
$20,000 annually into our Sidewalk Reserve Fund, the Town now has $25,000 annually 
put into its sidewalk fund. The Town now owns more sidewalks than the Fire District. 
The District simply does not have the resources to continue maintaining sidewalks as our 
revenues are declining and our costs are increasing.  Our Sidewalk Reserve Fund has 
been exhausted. The District's primary concern must be water. (If we had the funds we 
would chose to redo the Beaver Meadow Road sidewalk, not any sections of the  Main 
Street sidewalks.)  Ideally the Fire District would like the throw up the sidewalks at its 
Annual Meeting in January so that the Town could vote to accept the sidewalks in March.  
Phil will create a map of the sidewalks for the Selectboard.  
 
The warrants for June's payroll and payables were signed. A full set of written 
financial statements was handed out and reviewed by the Committee. The 
Committee voted unanimously to get a new phone and answering machine for the 
office and to move the FAX machine up to the shop. Jonathan will give office keys to 
Barbara and Vince.

controller for the pump that Bert Parrot recommends. This will cost either $3,000 or 
$4,000 and will be a true capitol improvement, like the VFD.  
 
After a lengthy discussion, the Committee voted unanimously to accept DR Key's bid 
to replace our 1922 mains and valves at the Hazen/Main Street intersection and to 
encourage them strongly to start as soon as possible.   
 
The Committee decided to tell Mr. Fraser he should go ahead and explore the feasibility 
of installing 400' of pipe from our main to his house at 137 Turnpike Road. The 
Committee voted unanimously, however, that no action may be taken until the 
Prudential Committee has reviewed and accepted the engineer's final plans. The 
Committee also authorized Brion to tell Mr. Fraser that he will not be billed for his 
first year's water. 
 
Jonathan's letter to Dr. Pinello about the former Moses house was reviewed. By 
unanimous vote the Committee forgave her bill for the first quarter. 
 
The Committee agreed to pay $100 a month into Sam's Family Insurance Supplement 
until the end of the year. We will look at a new policy for 2012. 
 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on August 15, 2011 in the small 
conference room in Tracy Hall at 5:30pm. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 8:17 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne H. French

                          PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
September 19, 2011 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Anne French 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:57 pm in the Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall, 
Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the August meeting were accepted as presented. 
 
Written financials for the first 6 months of 2011 were distributed. Questions were raised about 
health insurance and the payroll in the Treasurer's Report. The cost of repairing this summer's 
water main breaks will be capitalized under maintenance. Jill Haney, our office staff, needs to be 
given more than four hours a week soon or we'll lose her. So far we've only paid here $600-
$700, even though we budgeted $5,000 to pay here. There is plenty of work to keep her busy but 
she needs more training. We need to develop her job description for her and she needs to have 
her three-month job evaluation. When Brion is away, Jill can help provide continuity. So far Jill

Hopefully we will have an agreement, ready to be signed at our next meeting, with Norwich 
Associates for the gravel pit easement.  
 
The Carter appeal was granted, forgiving half the overage for the last quarter.

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
 
November 14, 2011                                                 DRAFT 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Cheryl 
Lindberg, Anne French, Auditor Priscilla Vincent 
 
The meeting was called to order at 6:05 pm in the Small Conference Room in Tracy 
Hall, Norwich, VT. 
The minutes of the October meeting were accepted as presented. 
The Prudential Committee discussed options for employee health insurance plans 
for Brion and Sam.  The Committee voted unanimously to level fund the health 
insurance line item in the 2012 budget. The Committee authorized Brion to pick a 
health plan and, if there were savings in the premiums, they would consider 
assisting employees with higher deductibles. 
In preparation for the 2012 budget, the Committee agreed that the following 
2011 expenses would be capitalized: replacement of the Main and Hazen Streets 
1922 water mains, replacement of the Koch Road water line, repair of the 5 water 
main breaks, and the upgrade to the VFD at the pump house. The Committee reviewed 
their existing 2005 bonding authority for $140,000 to replace the unlined 
tuberculated pipe. Brion estimates that it will cost $7,000 to install chemical 
feed pumps and continuous monitoring at the pump house when we are required to 
comply with the provisions of the groundwater rules. Brion has asked to stay at 
32 hours a week for the next budget year. 
The Prudential Committee members signed the notarized document for the Farrell 
Gravel Pit easement. 
From 6:15 - 6:25 the Prudential Committee met in Executive Session to discuss job 
evaluations. Following the session, the Committee voted unanimously to accept the 
evaluations. 
From 6:40 - 6:55 the Committee met in Executive Session to discuss Jill¹s review.  
Following the session, the Committee voted unanimously to accept the review. 
The Committee reviewed paper financial statements through the end October. 
With 95% of our 2011 taxes collected, the Fire District has not yet received 
payment from 17 customers.  A total of $3,108 in delinquent taxes are still due.  
The Committee is in the process of considering several issues. Among them are 
these: how to replenish the Capital Fund, the disposition of our sidewalks, the 
difference between the Town¹s cost of living rate (2.6%) and the Fire District¹s 
rate (2.2%), how to deal with the increased cost of health insurance, and the 
sharing of costs for hydrant protection with all who use the hydrants. It is a 
great challenge for the Prudential Committee that there are so many fixed costs 
for running a Water Department. For instance, in the near future, the District 
will have to buy 350 new meters ($200 each), software to accompany the meters 
($12,000), and a remote meter reader ($12,000).  
The Committee considered Jean Lenzner¹s appeal and decided, for now, to charge 
her what would be her average quarterly billing. A final decision will be made 
after better information about the situation is obtained. 
The next Prudential Committee meeting will be held on Monday, December 5, at 5:30 
pm, in the Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall. The budget for 2012 will be the 
only agenda item. The Annual Meeting will be held on January 23, 2012. 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:52 pm. 
Respectfully submitted, 
Anne H. French

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT         DRAFT 
                          PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
February 27, 2012 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullan, Cheryl Lindberg, Anne 
French, Priscilla Vincent, Jim Harlow, Dr. Susan Kowalski 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:30 pm in the Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall, 
Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the January meeting were accepted as presented. 
 
Jim Harlow, Commander of the Norwich American Legion, requested that the Legion be 
exempted from paying the minimum use charge which is equal to the cost of 3,800 gallons per 
quarter. The Prudential Committee is concerned about setting a precedent should the Legion be 
granted relief from this charge. Of our 350 connections, there are 41 that use under 3,800 
gallons per quarter and 17 that use under 2,000 gallons per quarter. We could gradually, over 
time, eliminate the minimum use fee while increasing the base rate.  After a lengthy discussion, 
the Prudential Committee unanimously voted to grant an exemption from the minimum 
use fee to the Legion and to the Grange. The Committee will be looking at a revision of all 
our rates at the Long Range Planning Meeting. 
 
Dr. Susan Kowalski came to the Prudential Committee to ask that we discontinue adding 
fluoride to our water supply. She presented the Committee with reading material supporting her 
request. She is opposed to fluoridation because the AMA considers fluoridation to be a medical 
treatment, Norwich citizens have no choice about receiving this treatment, and because of 
concerns about infants and toddlers drinking fluoridated water. The Committee decided the 
issue needs further research and will discuss it again at our next meeting.  
 
Treasurer Lindberg gave a verbal Treasurer's report and the January payables and payroll were 
reviewed and signed. 
 
The Committee voted unanimously to increase Bob Edmands' hourly wages by 0.35 cents 
and to further discuss increasing the employees' family benefits contribution to 80% of 
cost, retroactive to January 1, 
 
During a discussion about the transfer of our remaining sidewalks to the Town, the Committee 
agreed that the Town needs to write up a document about the transfer to be recorded  and kept 
with the Town records. 
 
DR Key Corp, L&M, Twin States, and Nott have been sent bids for the Main Street water main 
replacement. 
 

Concerning our proposed office staff position, Brion reiterated his feeling that we need an office 
person (more than strictly a book keeper) to work 4 hours a day on Mondays, Wednesdays and 
Friday. 
 
Brion and Jonathan will work on a letter to Mr. Turco about the swale crossing his land. As we 
appear to hold no easement for the swale on his property, we don't have any authority on this 
issue. We will give him recommendations on how to proceed and put him in touch  with the 
right people.  
 
Susan McCoy's appeal request about on/off charges was denied. Brion will write her a letter 
explaining the decision.  
 
The date for Long Range Planning Meeting was tentatively set for Wednesday, April 25. 
Among items on the agenda will be our office staff, water rates, and our financial capacity. Neil 
Fulton will be one of our guests. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:45pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne French 
Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT             DRAFT 
                          PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
March 19, 2012 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullan, Cheryl Lindberg, Anne 
French 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:37 pm in the Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall, 
Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the February meeting were accepted as presented with the addition of the word 
"warrants", following "payroll", in the third paragraph. The minutes of the 2012 Annual 
Meeting were reviewed. Cheryl will have written financials for the April meeting. The  March 
payables and payroll warrants were reviewed and signed. 
 
After a long discussion of family health benefits for full-time employees and their families, the 
Prudential Committee voted unanimously to fully fund Sam's monthly family premium 
for the year, beginning in April.  ($238 x9 = $2,142) The Committee also voted to give a 
one-time $500 bonus to both Sam and Brion to be used as cash or as a payment toward 
their HSA plan. In preparation for hiring future employees, the ultimate goal is to pay 
everybody's premium for short and long-term disability and dental. Future employees will be 
asked to have their spouse use their employer's insurance plan when possible. Next year we will 
have to look at the family health benefits issue again. 
 
The Prudential Committee conducted a lengthy consideration of fluoride in our drinking water. 
Everybody agreed that the entire District would need to be consulted before any policy changes 
might be made.  The Committee decided to send out a note to everybody with the next 
Confidence Report  (CCR) inviting Fire District residents with strong concerns, for or against 
fluoride, to send their comments to the Prudential Committee. The Committee voted 
unanimously to have Brion draft this note and bring it to the May meeting. We are in full 
compliance with the ADA recommendations and we do not use fluoride silicate, which is what 
most water systems studied in the negative reports are using.  
 
Three of the agenda items for the Long Range Planning Meeting are:  an 8:00 am inspection of 
parcels #2 and #3, the log-landing, and the shed; a review of our office staff accompanied by a 
written statement of job procedures; a review of  our capital planning. Some of the  comments 
made about the last item were: we need to know where we stand on the budget before 
December 30th; personnel evaluations should be done in June; catastrophic failures aren't our 
main concern since we only need enough money to hold ourselves over until we can go to the 
District for a bond vote; we need to reinstate the policy of putting $15,000 into the Capital 
Reserve Fund annually. Brion will send the PDF of the Town Personnel Policy to the Prudential 
Committee. 
 

The bids for replacing 1,200' of Main Street pipe have been received: 
 
L&M  
 
 $110,00 
 
Dana Key 
 
 $125,650 
 
Nott  
 
$ 141,640 
 
Twin State              did not bid 
The Town says it still doesn't know when it will repave and, as yet, has no plans or drawings. 
Brion says the replacement will never be cheaper than it is now. Total cost of the pipe 
replacement, including moving services, and setting up a contingency fund will be about 
$140,000. At Brion's recommendation, the Prudential Committee voted unanimously to 
accept L&M's  low bid and to proceed with the Main Street pipe replacement. L&M's bid 
is a "cost not to exceed bid ". They will start in May or June and expect to finish the job in 15-
20 working days, starting at the Library. They are hoping to maintain two lanes of traffic until 
they reach Uppper Hazen and will reopen two lanes of traffic at the end of each working day. 
 
Since we are dealing with increasing costs associated with water delivery, have a fixed revenue 
base, and only get an average of $500-$600 a year from each customer, we will need a loan to 
finance this work. The Committee voted unanimously to have Brion get updated figures 
from the banks. We hope a bank loan will not be as expensive as a loan through the Bond 
Bank. 
 
The next monthly meeting will be April 25th at 2:00 pm , following the Long Range Planning 
Meeting in the Norwich Inn, Norwich, VT. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:00 pm. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne French 
Clerk

Confidence Report  (CCR) inviting Fire District residents with strong concerns, for or against 
fluoride, to send their comments to the Prudential Committee. The Committee voted 
unanimously to have Brion draft this note and bring it to the May meeting. We are in full 
compliance with the ADA recommendations and we do not use fluoride silicate, which is what 
most water systems studied in the negative reports are using.  
 
Three of the agenda items for the Long Range Planning Meeting are:  an 8:00 am inspection of 
parcels #2 and #3, the log-landing, and the shed; a review of our office staff accompanied by a 
written statement of job procedures; a review of  our capital planning. Some of the  comments 
made about the last item were: we need to know where we stand on the budget before 
December 30th; personnel evaluations should be done in June; catastrophic failures aren't our 
main concern since we only need enough money to hold ourselves over until we can go to the 
District for a bond vote; we need to reinstate the policy of putting $15,000 into the Capital 
Reserve Fund annually. Brion will send the PDF of the Town Personnel Policy to the Prudential 
Committee. 
 

The bids for replacing 1,200' of Main Street pipe have been received: 
 
L&M  
 
 $110,00 
 
Dana Key 
 
 $125,650 
 
Nott  
 
$ 141,640 
 
Twin State              did not bid 
The Town says it still doesn't know when it will repave and, as yet, has no plans or drawings. 
Brion says the replacement will never be cheaper than it is now. Total cost of the pipe 
replacement, including moving services, and setting up a contingency fund will be about 
$140,000. At Brion's recommendation, the Prudential Committee voted unanimously to 
accept L&M's  low bid and to proceed with the Main Street pipe replacement. L&M's bid 
is a "cost not to exceed bid ". They will start in April with 20 men in two crews and expect to 
finish the job in 15-20 working days, starting at the Library. They will be working out of the 
roadway until they get to Upper Hazen and then are hoping to maintain two lanes of traffic until 
the job is finished.  
 
Since we are dealing with increasing costs associated with water delivery, have a fixed revenue 
base, and only get an average of $500-$600 a year from each customer, we will need a loan to 
finance this work. The Committee voted unanimously to have Brion get updated figures 
from the banks. A bank loan would not be as expensive as a loan from the bond bank. 
 
The next monthly meeting will be April 25th at 2:00 pm , following the Long Range Planning 
Meeting in the Norwich Inn, Norwich, VT. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:00 pm. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Anne French 
Clerk

                     PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
 
 
 
 
           September 24, 2012 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullan, Anne French,  
Priscilla Vincent  
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:26 p.m. in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT. 
 
The minutes of the August meeting were accepted as presented. 
 
Brion reported that Kimberly is working out well as our new administrative assistant. We still 
need to figure out what to do with our 160 cu.ft. of boxed records. They need to be stored in an 
accessible, dry place with even temperatures. Kim does not yet have access to the accounts 
payables in the computer. She would need this to update our vendor files.  Brion would like to 
review our chart of accounts.  
 
The Fire District has received a $2,000 PACIF grant for safety cones, a line locator, and other 
safety equipment.  
 
The Committee reviewed the process of developing our budget. Brion needs the final figures for 
the mailing 10 days before the Annual Meeting. The Committee agreed to move the personnel 
reviews to the Spring, so as not to interfere with the budget process. Brion hopes that this will 
be the year we initiate a more efficient, effective system for setting up our budget. Everybody 
agreed that there is no point in reviewing the budget until early December, when we have our 
year-end figures. We should use prior meetings to discuss budget policies.  This year the 
Repairs and Maintenance category will need to be expanded to $10,000-$15,000. Any surplus, 
at year's end, could be rolled into the capital fund. The Committee heard taxpayer complaints 
regarding our 2012 tax bill.

December 17, 2012 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullen, Cheryl Lindberg, Anne 
French, Kim Edgar 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:34 p.m. in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT.

Committee.

budget meeting in January. 
 
The Committee voted unanimously to stay with the same health insurance plan for full-time employees. 
The annual cost, including HSA, is $17,450. 
 
The Annual Meeting Warning will be mailed on January 18th. 
 
The next meeting of the Prudential Committee will be held on Monday, January 7, at 5:30 p.m., in the 
Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall. The Annual Meeting will be held on January 28, 2013, at 7:30 
p.m. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 8:25 p.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted,

Present:  Prudential Committee Chair Jonathan Vincent, Prudential Committee 
Members Michael Goodrich and Alicia Groft, also Water Operator Tim Cronan, 
Barbara Currier, Operations Manager Sam Eaton, Deirdre Goodrich, Treasurer 
Cheryl Lindberg and Auditor Priscilla Vincent. 
 
The meeting was called to order at 7:50 p.m. in the Multi-purpose Room at Tracy 
Hall, following the Norwich Fire District's 2018 Annual Meeting. 
 
1.  Michael Goodrich was unanimously elected Chair of the Norwich Fire District. 
 
2.  Jonathan Vincent gave the Prudential Committee his resignation with one       
year still remaining on his elected Prudential Committee position. 
 
3.  Prudential Committee members Michael Goodrich and Alicia Groft accepted 
his resignation. 
 
2.  Vincent offered to serve in the unfilled position of Fire District Clerk. 
 
3.  Michael Goodrich, Chair, and Alicia Groft appointed Vincent as the new Fire 
District Clerk. 
 
4.  Barbara Currier graciously agreed to serve on the Prudential Committee for 
the one remaining year on Vincent's term, subject to approval by the Norwich 
Select Board. 
 
5.  It was agreed that Vincent's letter of resignation and the recommendation that 
the unfilled position be filled by Barbara Currier be presented to the Norwich 
Select Board prior to their next scheduled meeting on February 14, 2018. 
 
6.  The next regular Norwich Fire District meeting was scheduled for February 
26, 2018 at 5:30 p.m. in the small Conference Room at Tracy Hall. 
 
7.  The meeting was adjourned by unanimous consent at 7:56 p.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Jonathan Vincent, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
FEB.26, 2018 
 
Present:  PC voting members: Barbara Currier, Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Clerk: Jonathan 
Vincent, Operations: Sam Eaton, Tim Cronan, Auditor: Priscilla Vincent 
 
The meeting was called to order at 6:31PM in the Tracy Hall Small Conference Room.   
 
The Prudential Committee unanimously voted to approve the Agenda for the February 
meeting as well as the Minutes of the January 22, 2018 meeting with one minor edit. 
 
There were no public comments. 
 
The Treasurer was not able at attend, but the financials had been distributed and there were 
no further comments. 
 
Mr. Eaton presented the operations report.   
• 
Meters are being read and backflow preventers inspected.  So far, about 115 
connections have been checked. 
• 
A sanitary survey was done at the reservoir.  One hatch was opened, and the gasket 
damaged due to cold weather conditions. 
• 
The Owner's Manual for equipment at the Pump House is being updated. 
• 
Competent Person Training is being arranged in April, subsidized by Ferguson 
Waterworks.  20 attendees are required for a special $100.00 per person rate. 
• 
Mike Tebbetts will be visiting the Kennedy Hydrant factory in March in Elmira, NY. 
• 
A ROV inspection of the cistern is planned; this will cost around $1,000.00. 
• 
Water bills were sent out, and there were only 26 Second Notices required. 
 
The operations report was unanimously approved with thanks to all involved. 
 
The Darrell Thompson Easement request was discussed.  The sense of the Prudential 
Committee was not to approve the requested 50 feet, a critical number to establish legal 
access.  Chair Michael Goodrich will contact Jack Candon and discuss whether a one or two 
rod access would be more appropriate, since enforcement of legal restrictions has been a 
problem in the past. 
 
Abatements of $131.51 for Marcus Ratliff and $123.77 for Jim and Donna Mackall were 
approved by the Prudential Committee.  
 
The Long Range Planning Meeting was discussed.  It tentatively is scheduled for April 11, 2018 
at 3:00 PM in the new Public Safety Building Conference/Training room. 
 
The next meeting of the Prudential Committee will be held on Monday March 19 at 5:30PM in 
the Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 6:30 PM. 
 
Jonathan Vincent, Clerk

the treasurer and the Water Department will develop a regular schedule for office computer

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT 
DRAFT PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
JULY 23, 2018 
 
Present:  PC Voting members: Michael Goodrich, Barbara Currier, Alicia Groft; 
Treasurer: Cheryl Lindberg; Water Department: Tim Cronan; Auditor: Priscilla 
Vincent; Land Management Council: Dave Hubbard; Clerk: Jonathan Vincent 
 
1.  The meeting was called to order at 5:30 P.M.  
 
2.  The Agenda was approved with amendments. 
 
3.  The June 18, 2018 Minutes were approved as amended. 
 
4.  Dave Hubbard explained that the stone Brown School House Road bridge 
had collapsed, and the Town had removed the debris.  There is a 19 foot gap, 
but an alternate trail down and across has been flagged.  Work repairing foot 
bridges on the Ballard Trail has started, thanks to a grant from the Norwich 
Women's Club.  Professional help is needed to repair damage to "The Stairway 
to Heaven," and the PC approved the LMC spending some of its $13,841.00 from 
logging receipts for this work. 
 
5.  Preliminary Grand List amounts indicate that the 2017 tax rate of .07 per 
$100.00 of assessed value would be sufficient, and the PC approved setting the 
2018 Fire District Tax Rate at the same amount.   
 
6. The PC approved a Zoning Permit to remove the rest of the Blood Brook dam. 
 
7.  Tim Cronan gave the Operations Report in Sam Eaton's absence.  Money has 
been raised to replace the dam.  Jack Candon feels that the Fire District cannot 
simply sell the Water Department to the Town, while retaining ownership of the 
Watershed Protection Lands.  The PC moved to begin discussions with Herb 
Durfee about the possible future transfer of the Fire District to the Town. 
 
8.  A car destroyed the hydrant at the bottom of Partridge Hill, and the protective 
bollards will have to be reset.  A new water service was installed to the Grange 
and the house behind it, and an old Ludlow hydrant on Beaver Meadow Road is 
scheduled for replacement. 
 
9.  The next PC Meeting is scheduled for August 27 at 5:30 P.M. 
 
10. The meeting adjourned at 6:50 P.M. 
 
 
Jonathan Vincent, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
SEPTEMBER 17, 2018 
 
Present:  PC Voting members: Michael Goodrich, Barbara Currier, Alicia Groft; 
Treasurer: Cheryl Lindberg; Water Department: Sam Eaton, Tim Cronan; Clerk: 
Jonathan Vincent; Selectboard: Linda Cook, John Langhus; Town Manager: 
Herb Durfee; Elliot Harick 
 
1.  The meeting was called to order at 5:32 P.M.  
 
2.  The Agenda was approved. 
 
3.  The August 27, 2018 Minutes were approved with one correction. 
 
4. The history of the Fire District was discussed.  For many years the Town paid 
the Norwich Fire District for Fire Department expenses. In the early 1980s the 
Fire Department became part of the Town.  The possible merger of the Fire 
District with the Town was discussed. 
 
5.  John Langhus questioned the financial status of the Fire District.  He was told 
that it is fine now, but that less than one third of the residents are paying the 
entire cost of public water, sized for fire protection. 
 
6. Linda Cook opposed a proposal to share bookkeeping with the Town.  
 
7. The Treasurer's report was given and accepted.  Payroll warrants for 9/19/18 
were approved and signed. 
 
8. The VLCT Ethics Conduct Policy was adopted. 
 
9.  Roberta refused to pay the interest on an invoice to the Town for "hydrant 
rental." This will be discussed with Herb Durfee (who had left). 
 
10.  The hydrant on Route 5 has been replaced, and dam removal is proceeding 
on Charles Brown Brook.  It appears the solar project will be delayed until Spring. 
A new hydrant was installed on Route 5. 
 
11.  A 4.65% increase from BCBS is expected; a draft budget will be prepared for 
discussion and revision at the next meeting. 
 
12.  The next PC Meeting is scheduled for October 22 at 5:30 P.M. 
 
13. The meeting adjourned at 6:43 P.M. 
 
Jonathan Vincent, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
OCTOBER 22. 2018 
 
Present:  PC Voting members: Michael Goodrich, Barbara Currier, Alicia Groft; 
Treasurer: Cheryl Lindberg; Water Department: Sam Eaton, Tim Cronan (part-
time); Auditor; Priscilla Vincent; Clerk: Jonathan Vincent; Jennifer Robie. 
 
1.  The meeting was called to order at 5:28 p.m. 
 
2.   Action on next year's VLCT insurance renewal was added to the Agenda at 
Cheryl Lindberg's request.  The Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved 
unanimously as amended. 
 
3.  The minutes from the September 17, 2018 meeting were corrected as follows: 
Elliott "Harack" is "Harik," in Item 9. Roberta refused to pay the interest on the 
invoice on the "hydrant rental," and the new hydrant in Item 10. was on Route 5.  
The Minutes were moved and approved unanimously with the above corrections. 
 
4.   Cheryl Lindberg noted that, in her opinion, the minutes should reflect motions 
and votes as recorded, according to the Vermont Open Meeting Law. 
 
5.  At 5:34 p.m. Executive Session was moved and approved to discuss 
personnel Issues.  Tim Cronan was invited to attend. 
 
6.  At 6:02 p.m. the meeting was back in session, with no action taken by the 
Prudential Committee. 
 
7.  The Treasurer presented a warrant for payables for the month of October.  
This was moved, approved, and voted unanimously by the Prudential Committee. 
 
8.  The Treasurer noted that the VLCT insurance needed to be reviewed and 
approved for 2019.  This includes Property, Casualty, Workers' Compensation, 
and Public Official Liability.  The PC noted that the dam was removed by 
10/19/2018, and so no insurance was needed.  Barbara Currier moved to adopt 
the insurance as amended, seconded by Michael Goodrich, and unanimously 
approved by the Prudential Committee. 
 
9.  Sam Eaton reported that Blue Cross-Blue Shield of Vermont projected a 
5.46% increase in rates for 2019.   
 
10.  The Prudential Committee moved, seconded, and agreed to bill Solar 
Technologies for the legal work performed by Jack Candon for the Fire District. 
 
11.  Legal fees for the 2019 Budget were increased to $1,000.00 per the 
Prudential Committee's motion, second, and approval. 

 
12.  The "Hydrant Rental Fee" to the Town was set at $18,000.00.  This is really 
for Fire Protection, and the Prudential Committee moved, seconded and 
approved renaming it "Town Fire Protection," since the entire system is sized to 
provide adequate water to fight fires not for domestic service. 
 
13.  Sam Eaton summarized the remaining portions of the 2006 engineering plan 
for replacing aging pipes with rough estimates for cost as follows: 
 
Trumbull Lane  
 
$35,000 
 
Hopson Road 
 
$150,00 
 
Elm Street 
 
 
$150,000 
 
Cliff and Hazen Streets 
$350,000 
 
14.  Sam Eaton also noted that in a year or two another truck would be required.  
He suggested a Reserve Fund to put money aside for this purpose each year; 
the total cost for a used truck might be $30,000.00. 
 
15.  Sam Eaton reported that the insurance company had paid for the destroyed 
hydrant, that the dam had been removed, and plants and trees will be planted 
next Spring.  The Asset Management Grant should be applied for as early as 
possible next year: 12:01 a.m. on January 1, 2019 was proposed.  Apparently 
three towns are also interested in this grant, and it is awarded on a first come 
basis.   Alicia Groft will attend an upcoming Asset Management Class, and 
November financials will acceptable for the initial application. 
 
16.  Flushing is almost complete, and the reservoir inspection will be done on 
10/27/2018 at a cost of $700.00.  Larry Wiggins, the new Norwich DPW Director, 
is working cooperatively with the Fire District. 
 
17.  Acceptance of the Report was moved by Barbara Currier, seconded by 
Michael Goodrich, and unanimously approved by the Prudential Committee. 
 
18.  Cooperation with the Town was discussed.  Mike Tebbetts will be running 
the sidewalk snow blower.  It is yet to be decided exactly how he will be paid. 
 
19.  The next Prudential Committee Meetings will be held November 12 and 
December 17, 2018 at 5:30 p.m. in Tracy Hall. 
 
20.  The Prudential Committee went into Executive Session at 7:06 p.m. to 
discuss personnel issues.  They ended at 7:31 p.m. with no action taken. 
 
Jonathan Vincent, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT              
                          PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES  
     October 7th, 2013 
 
Present: Jonathan Vincent, Barbara Currier, Vince Watts, Brion McMullan,  
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:45 in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT 
 
Regular business 
The minutes of the September meeting were accepted.  
 
The Treasurer presented September financial reports. Expenditures associated with the pump 
house fire tally to approximately $35,000 with an additional $15,000 spent but still outstanding. 
Cheryl has requested and expects a check from the VLCT soon. Cheryl reported BCA 
adjustment on Town warrant for Fire District and if we are successful we will receive additional 
funding thru Board of Abatement. 
 
Administrator's Report - Solarflect easement - Committee requested Brion inquire on economic 
incentives to host and whether Solarflect would consider allowing District to be part of their 
security system. 
 
Current business 
Committee voted to pursue Alternate #2with metal siding and metal roof and underground 
piping option with removal of back addition. Brion to request final design estimate for these 
items and discuss going with smaller pump and motor on well #1. Brion to ask Dufresne cost 
difference between design/build and design/bid/build. Due to time of year, the Committee voted 
not to enter into a design/build agreement with Trumbull-Nelson; but, instead consider 
developing bid documents over the winter and go out to bid in early 2014. Brion to inform 
Trumbull and Dufresne. 
  
The next meeting of the Prudential Committee will be held on Monday, October 28th  at 5:30,  
in the Small Conference Room in Tracy Hall, Norwich, VT. Treasurer to provide draft budget 
sheets and Committee to discuss those expenditure items likely to impact next year's budget. 
The meeting was adjourned at 8pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Brion McMullan, District Administrator

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
JANUARY 27, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Clerk:  Steve Allen 
 
The meeting was called to order at 8:18 p.m. 
1. The January 27, 2020 Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously. 
 
2. Michael Goodrich was nominated to the post of Chairman. Moved, seconded, and 
approved unanimously. 
 
3. It was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously the Accounts Payable warrants 
20-01 for the General Fund and the Water Fund. 
 
4. Items were suggested for discussion at the next meeting: 
-- Priorities for 2020 
-- Status of the merger talks with the town of Norwich 
-- Personnel policy 
-- Asset management plan 
-- Timeline for decisions 
 
5. The time and date of the next meeting was proposed as February 17, 2020 at 3:30 
p.m. Moved, seconded, and approved unanimously. 
 
6. The PC adjourned the meeting at 8:32. 
 
 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
October 13, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts; Clerk:  Steve Allen; Public:  Priscilla Vincent, Linda Cook 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:02 p.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, this was virtual and conducted by teleconference. Lindberg expressed her regrets that she 
could not attend the meeting. 
  
1. The day's agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
2. The minutes from the Sept. 28 meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
3. There were no comments during the public comments section; 
 
4. There was a discussion of whether NFD staff should have debit/credit cards in order to make 
small purchases - it was moved, seconded, and approved to move ahead on setting up debit or 
credit cards, which kind of card to be decided later; 
 
5. The operations report mentioned a letter received from the Town of Norwich Fire Chief 
regarding "two vulnerable areas of need regarding water supply and town fire defense" - this 
letter will be discussed at the next meeting of the NFD PC; 
 
6. There were ongoing discussions of the budget and how to responsibly fund fire district priorities. 
 
7. The next PC meeting date was agreed to be October 26 at 5:00 p.m., with the main agenda 
item to be further discussion of the 2021 budget; 
 
8. It was moved, seconded, and approved for the PC to go into Executive Session. Personnel 
issues were discussed, no action was taken. It was moved, seconded, and approved to leave 
Executive Session.  
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 6:31 p.m.

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
October 26, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Clerk:  Steve Allen; Public:  Priscilla 
Vincent, Linda Cook 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:02 p.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, this was virtual and conducted by teleconference.  
  
1. The day's agenda was moved, seconded, and approved with the addition of a vote on a payroll 
warrant; 
 
2. The minutes from the Oct. 13 meeting were discussed, action deferred until next meeting; 
 
3. Vincent asked about logging operations undertaken by the Norwich Land Commission on NFD 
property. The Water Department responded that the Commission has been reminded that this 
requires prior permission; 
 
4. There was a discussion of a new water connection for 81 Cliff Street, a property that was 
recently subdivided into two parcels. The new water connection was moved, seconded, and 
approved; 
 
5. There was further discussion of the NFD credit/debit card policy, based on a document sent to 
PC members from the Treasurer on Oct. 20. It was moved, seconded, and approved to adopt 
this policy with two changes:  a) the cards will be debit cards, b) an alert system will be 
established to ensure that the Treasurer sees any unusual activity; 
 
6. There was a discussion of the VLTC insurance renewal application, and whether the NFD's lack 
of specific policies on certain issues results in higher rates; Lindberg thinks not, and the 
application was moved, seconded, and approved as presented;  
 
7. There were ongoing discussions of the budget and how to responsibly fund fire district priorities. 
 
8. There was a discussion of Treasury issues, including a what to do with the $126,500 CD that is 
maturing; it was decided for now to put the funds into an account paying 0.6% interest per year. 
A payroll warrant was moved, seconded, and approved. 
 
9. There was ongoing discussion of the letter from the Norwich Fire Chief requesting the extension 
of water lines on Highway 5 South; 
 

10. The next PC meeting dates were agreed to be Nov. 9 at 4:00 p.m. and Nov. 23 at 5:00 p.m., 
with the main agenda item to be further discussion of the 2021 budget; 
 
11. It was moved, seconded, and approved for the PC to go into Executive Session. Personnel 
issues were discussed, no action was taken. It was moved, seconded, and approved to leave 
Executive Session.  
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 6:28 p.m. 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
November 23, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Auditor:  Priscilla Vincent; Clerk:  Steve 
Allen; Norwich Fire Chief Alex Northern; Public:  Linda Cook 
The meeting was called to order at 5:02 p.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, this was virtual and conducted by teleconference.  
  
1. The day's agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as amended to include a discussion of 
the annual meeting; 
 
2. The minutes from the Nov. 9 meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as amended to 
include statute citations in the motion to move to Executive Session; it was discussed whether in 
future to include full versions of the Operations and Treasurer's Reports in the minutes; 
 
3. There were no public comments; 
 
4. The Norwich Fire Chief Alex Northern discussed his previous letter to the PC regarding potential 
expansion of NFD water mains to areas not currently included in the district. It was decided that 
one or more members of the PC should discuss the matter with the Norwich Town Manager; 
 
5. The treasurer's report noted that approximately $5,000 of outstanding taxes have not yet been 
paid; the treasurer's report was moved, seconded, and approved as amended to include the 
signing of Accounts Payable and Payroll warrants; 
 
6. The operations report noted that repairs to the NFD's damaged building on Beaver Meadow 
Road are complete, and also that an updated personnel policy requires new PC signatures; 
 
7. There were ongoing discussions of the 2021 budget, including how to choose the appropriate 
index for cost of living increases and the cost of an outside audit for the NFD; 
 
8. The annual meeting was discussed, including the possibility that due to voting and procedural 
changes that may be required, the date of the meeting may have to be postponed from January 
25 to a later date. A number of questions were discussed that Allen will ask of the Vermont 
Secretary of State's office on elections; 
 
9. The next PC meeting date was agreed to be Dec. 7 at 5:00 p.m., with the main agenda items to 
be further discussion of the 2021 budget, the annual meeting, and an executive session to 
discuss personnel issues; 
 
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 6:21 p.m. 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
November 9, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Clerk:  Steve Allen; Public:  Priscilla 
Vincent 
 
The meeting was called to order at 4:04 p.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, this was virtual and conducted by teleconference.  
  
1. The day's agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
2. The minutes from the Oct. 13 meeting and the Oct. 26 meeting were moved, seconded, and 
approved as amended; 
 
3. There were no public comments; 
 
4. The operations report noted that the NFD's new truck and plow have been purchased, and also 
that arrangements are being made for the Norwich Fire Chief to speak to the PC; the operations 
report was moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
5. The treasurer's report noted that $6,200 of outstanding taxes have not yet been paid, and that 
$600 of penalties and interest have accrued on this sum so far; the treasurer's report was 
moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
6. The date and time for the annual general meeting were set as 25 January at 7 p.m.; there was a 
discussion of how best to conduct the vote, with the Clerk directed to contact VLTC for 
suggestions; 
 
7. There were ongoing discussions of the 2021 budget, including how to present information in 
order to ensure transparency; 
 
8. The next PC meeting date was agreed to be Nov. 23 at 5:00 p.m., with the main agenda item to 
be further discussion of the 2021 budget; 
 
9. It was moved by the Chair, seconded, and approved for the PC to find that premature general 
public knowledge regarding the Fire District's review of an employee would clearly place the 
employee at a substantial disadvantage. It was then - under the provisions of Title 1, Section 
313(a)(3) of the Vermont Statutes - moved by the Chair, seconded, and approved for the PC to 
go into Executive Session to discuss the annual review of an employee and invite the 
bookkeeper to join the session. Personnel issues were discussed, no action was taken. It was 
moved, seconded, and approved to leave Executive Session at 5:40 p.m.  
 

 
  
The PC returned to public session at 5:40 pm and no action was taken. 
  
 
It was moved, seconded, and approved that the PC adjourn the meeting at 5:41 p.m. 
Steve Allen, Clerk
