NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
December 7, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft; Water Department:  Sam Eaton, 
Mike Tebbetts; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Auditor:  Priscilla Vincent; Clerk:  Steve Allen; 
Public:  Linda Cook 
The meeting was called to order at 5:04 p.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, this was virtual and conducted by teleconference.  
  
1. The day's agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
2. The minutes from the Nov. 23 meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as amended to 
include some changes in wording;  
 
3. There were no public comments; 
 
4. Conclusions from the Open Meeting Law Seminar were discussed. The main conclusions were 
that PC members should not discuss among themselves, outside of PC meetings, any topics 
that may be voted on in the future, and separately that Executive Sessions should only be used 
for discussion of specified topics, not topics for general (open) discussion; 
 
5. An abatement request on the water bill for 18 Moore Lane was discussed. An extra 43,800 
gallons of water were used because of a leak that took place over 90 days in the Spring; the 
extra usage was not related to the homemade ice rink that sits on the property now, despite how 
it looks. It was moved, seconded, and approved to grant the requested abatement of $184.43; 
 
6. How to conduct the annual meeting given Covid-related safety restrictions was discussed. 
Various ideas were considered, including whether to hold a traditional floor meeting or to hold a 
meeting using the Australian ballot. It was moved, seconded, and approved to change the 
method of holding the meeting and voting to an Australian ballot; 
 
7. The 2021 budget was discussed and the PC agreed to finalize it at the next meeting; 
 
8. The next PC meeting date was agreed to be Dec. 21 at 5:00 p.m., with the main agenda items 
to be further discussion of the 2021 budget and the annual meeting; 
 
9. It was moved by the Chair, seconded, and approved for the PC to find that premature general 
public knowledge regarding the Fire District's review of an employee would place the employee 
at a substantial disadvantage. It was then - under the provisions of Title 1, Section 313(a)(3) of 
the Vermont Statutes - moved by the Chair, seconded, and approved for the PC to go into 
Executive Session to discuss the annual review of an employee at 5:52 p.m. Personnel issues 
were discussed. It was moved, seconded, and approved to leave Executive Session at 6:07 
p.m. It was moved, seconded, and approved to give all three NFD employees a 3% annual 
salary increase. 
 
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 6:08 p.m. 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
FEBRUARY 17, 2020 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Clerk:  Steve Allen 
 
The meeting was called to order at 3:35 p.m. 
 
1. The February 17, 2020 Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously, 
after adding an item to sign a corrected January warrant. 
 
2. The corrected minutes from the January 27, 2020 meeting were approved 
unanimously. 
 
3. Treasurer's report: 
-- Discussion of the solar project, how much money it is saving, how the economics work; 
-- Discussion of reserve funds put into CD's at Mascoma Bank; 
-- Having committee members sign corrected documents relating to a January payroll 
warrant, as well as a February payroll warrant and a February accounts payable warrant 
for the General Fund and the Water Fund; 
-- PC members voted unanimously to approve the warrants. 
-- Lindberg provided an update to the PC on the NEMRC license and support 
agreements.  
 
4. Operations report: 
-- Discussion of current operations:  no leaks, higher-than-usual usage (90,000 gallons vs 
typical 80,000), annual backflow testing for businesses, truck fuel pump had to be fixed, 
there are 30 remaining unpaid water bills;  
-- Discussion of water meters to be purchased, and whether the decision should be put out 
for bids using an RFP process; 
-- Discussion of new truck to be purchased, and whether it should use an RFP or a simple 
spec list. It was agreed that both the water meters and the truck will use an RFP, drafts to 
be examined at the next meeting; 
-- Discussion of when RFP's should be used and whether those rules should be included 
in an official financial policy for the fire district. 
-- There was an update from Sam on the Asset Management Plan and dates selected to 
meet with Dufresne Group to discuss final document. 

 
5. It was agreed to examine the priorities for 2020 in the following order: 
-- Job descriptions 
-- Personnel policy 
-- The division of the budget into specific funds 
-- Potential merger of assets with the town of Norwich 
-- Asset management plan 
-- Hiring 
-- Financial policy 
-- Performance reviews 
-- It was also agreed to set a working group meeting for March 2, 2020 at 3:30 pm to 
discuss these issues in more depth. 
 
6. Corrections to job descriptions were discussed, ideas will be sent out for comments. 
 
7. Corrections to the personnel policy were discussed, through section 17 of the 
document; to continue from that point at the next meeting. 
 
8. Request will be made to the LMC to provide an update in the near future to the 
Prudential Committee on any recent activity. 
 
9. The time and date of the next meeting was proposed as March 23, 2020 at 3:30 p.m. 
Moved, seconded, and approved unanimously. 
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 5:24. 
 
 
Steve Allen, Clerk

Water Department: Sam Eaton 
Regrets 
PC Member: Elliot Harik 
1. Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 8:04am. 
2. Approval of Agenda: A motion to approve the Agenda as presented was made, seconded, voted 
unanimous. 
3. Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes: The minutes from the September 14th meeting, including changes 
proposed by Lindberg, were discussed. A motion to approve the minutes, as amended, was made, 
seconded, and voted unanimous. 
4. Public Comment: There were no public comments.  
5. Conservation Committee: As Will Haslett was not present at the meeting, there was no Conservation 
Committee discussion.

also noted that there will be modest additional revenue in the 4th quarter resulting from collections of penalties 
and interest due from delinquent taxpayers. A motion to approve the Treasurer's Report was made, 
seconded, and voted unanimous. 
7. Operations Report: A motion to approve the Operations Report was made, seconded, and voted 
unanimous.  
8. Discussion of Hazen & Cliff Street Project / Discussion of Budget: There was discussion over how to 
fund and when to complete the Hazen and Cliff Street project. The project is roughly estimated to cost 
~$500k, and the ideal time to perform the work may be next spring. The current reserve fund is greater than 
its historical average level and could be used to fund a portion of the project. There was discussion about 
soliciting input from local banks on a potential loan amount and interest rate for the project. Lindberg will 
inquire and the project funding & timing conversation will continue after receiving a read on potential debt 
financing. There was also general discussion of the budget process, including conversation about ~$20k of 
upcoming cost to replace meters in 2022. There was further discussion about asking the Selectboard to 
consider allocating some of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (ARPA) funds received by Norwich to 
fund Fire District projects. 
9. Discussion of Merger: The merger discussion was deferred to a future meeting. 
10. Discussion of RFP for Audit: October 29th is the deadline for auditors to respond to the PC's Request for 
Proposal (RFP) for a potential Audit of the Fire District's financials. Lindberg and Groft agreed to meet on 
the 29th at 4pm to open the responses and initiate a review of the proposals. Goodrich will join if available.

12. Determination of Next Meeting: The date and time for the next PC meeting was set Tuesday, November 
2nd at 8am at a place to be determined.

9:09am.

PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
December 6, 2021 
Present 
Prudential Committee (PC) Members: Michael Goodrich (Chair), Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik 
Treasurer: Cheryl Lindberg 
Clerk: Daniel Officer 
Water Department: Sam Eaton, Michael Tebbetts 
Auditor: Priscilla Vincent

1. Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 3:31pm. 
2. Approval of Agenda: A motion to approve the Agenda as presented was made, seconded, and voted 
unanimously. 
3. Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes: A motion to approve the minutes from the November 2, 2021 meeting 
was made, seconded, and voted unanimously. 
4. Public Comment: There were no public comments.  
5. Treasurer's Report: Lindberg noted there remain some delinquent taxpayers. Lindberg also indicated that 
the Fire District recently received new quotes for 2022 from VLCT for workers comp and various insurance 
rates. These will flow into the 2022 budget. There was renewed discussion about the proposed audit of the 
Fire District's financials. At the last meeting, the PC expressed surprise at the audit quote that resulted from 
the recent RFP process and the PC agreed to research comparable audit expenses for other fire districts. 
Goodrich reported that, following the last meeting, he spoke to another Vermont fire district. Goodrich learned 
that the other fire district hires a CPA to complete an annual audit of their books at a rate which helped to 
contextualize the PC's recently received quote for a one-time audit. Following Goodirch's update, there was 
continued discussion about whether the PC needs an audit. A motion to approve the Treasurer's Report was 
made, seconded, and voted unanimously. 
6. Budget Discussion: There was discussion around the draft 2022 budget. The PC renewed the conversation 
around the Hazen & Cliff project and revisited the topic of whether this project can be eligible for a portion of 
Norwich's ARPA funds. Harik emailed a representative of the Selectboard for an update on when the 
Selectboard will consider the PC's request for ARPA funds. The outcome of the ARPA fund discussion will 
help to determine the amount and type of financing required to complete the Hazen & Cliff project and will 
thus impact the 2022 budget. The PC discussed many of the other budgeted line items and contemplated 
an increase to hydrant fees. The PC agreed for Lindberg and Tebbetts to revisit some of the line-item 
assumptions, and the PC agreed to resume the budget discussion at the next meeting.

restrictions.

December 17th.

increase.

in the future. 
 
7. The issue of who will pay to maintain the sidewalks owned by the NFD was 
discussed. The Norwich Town Manager will talk to the PC at the long-term meeting 
in May, and it was pointed out that since the sidewalks are in the right of way of the 
town, there is logic to the town maintaining them. Harik mentioned that mailboxes are 
also in the town's right of way, but when they damage them during plowing they don't 
take responsibility for repairing them. Lindberg replied that the town does repair 
them, but Harik said that he called the town five times and never got a response, so 
had to fix it himself.   

 
8. The topic of recently approved Federal infrastructure spending was discussed. Eaton 
pointed out that the funds are intended specifically for new infrastructure, not 
replacement projects. Several ideas were considered, including whether it would be 
cost effective to extend a line of X meters to only Y houses, given state requirements 
on pipe diameters and hydrant inter-distances; also the future maintenance costs of 
infrastructure built with grant money now; also what constitutes a "shovel-ready" 
project (engineering done, plan approved by state); also whether the new water 
meters can be considered to be new infrastructure due to the technology component. 
Eaton will look into these questions and the discussion will continue in the future.  
 
9. The date for the next PC meeting was set as April 27th at 8:00 a.m., with the agenda 
to cover the question of infrastructure spending, the agenda and date of the long-
term meeting, and the Treasurer's report. This was moved, seconded, and approved 
unanimously. 
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 10:01 a.m. 
 
 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
April 27, 2021 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Auditor:  Priscilla Vincent; Clerk:  Steve 
Allen 
The meeting was called to order at 8:07 a.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, 2020 this was virtual and conducted by teleconference.  
 
1. The day's Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as amended to include a 
discussion of the Treasurer's report. 
 
2. The minutes from the April 20th meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as 
presented. 
 
3. In the public comments section, Lindberg asked some questions about the decision 
on water meters, speaking as a resident and not as Treasurer. She was surprised 
that the decision was made to commit to purchasing only one-third of the meters 
from one vendor; she has not experienced this idea of dividing a single project into 
thirds, and thinks that it will undermine the effectiveness of the RFP process. Why 
not install all the meters at once, and use a contractor for labor if that's necessary? 
Eaton said that due to an issue with the batteries to be used, it's best not to install 
them all at once, and vendors will not guarantee a meter price several years in the 
future. Since we don't want to see the entire group of meters fail at around the same 
time, their purchase will be staggered in 3 year periods. He also said that they looked 
into installing all of the meters with a contractor, and estimated that it would cost 
three times as much as to buy the meters in thirds. Harik said that there are risks if 
it's done either way, in thirds or all at once, and he doesn't think it's strange to make 
the purchase in tranches. 
 
4. The Treasurer's report was discussed, including funds that may be available for 
dismantling solar arrays and insurance certificates' expiration dates. This includes 
receiving an annual bank statement for the funds that are available for the 
decommissioning of the solar array and new insurance certificates for the insurance 
that the lessor is required to maintain during the leasing of the Fire District land. The 
PC voted to approve the report. 
 
5. The discussion of potential infrastructure funds from the state was continued. Eaton 
said that he spoke to some people from the state, and they told him that the situation 
is not settled yet - the total amount that will be available is still unclear, and whether 
replacement infrastructure will be eligible has not yet been decided. It should be 
clearer in a few weeks. Harik suggested that the PC find out as much as possible 

about the process and invite a state representative to speak about it at the long 
range meeting. Goodrich said that he will find out if that is possible and get back to 
the PC. 
 
6. The long range meeting was discussed. Goodrich proposed that the agenda start 
with those items he suggested in March:   
- Merger of assets with the Town of Norwich 
- Application of Asset Management Plan 
- Review NFD land lease with town 
- Start replacing meters 
- Audit  
 
Harik said that all suggestions should be put into a laundry list, including possibly to 
invite the town manager to discuss a merger, and a state representative or senator to 
discuss infrastructure spending. Lindberg asked what was meant by "merger", and 
whether that was too suggestive of a business transaction. Does it mean the NFD 
being taken over by the town? Or does it mean turning over an "enterprise function" 
to the town? Harik suggested defining the merger as an "absorption" or a 
"dissolution". Lindberg said that if that is the case, there needs to be a large 
discussion about the land owned by the NFD. Harik suggested adding the topic of 
land management to the long range meeting. It was discussed whether to invite other 
people, including the fire chief and an engineer who worked on the asset 
management plan, and decided in the negative.  
 
7. The date for the next PC meeting was set as May 11th at 9:00 a.m., with the agenda 
to include more discussion of the long range meeting and a presentation from LMT 
Land Management.  
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 9:06 a.m. 
 
 
Steve Allen, Clerk

PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
May 11, 2021

Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Clerk:  Steve Allen; Public:  Linda Cook 
The meeting was called to order at 9:01 a.m. As has been the case for all meetings after March 
2, 2020 this was virtual and conducted by teleconference.  
 
1. The day's Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented. 
 
2. The minutes from the April 27th meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as 
amended. 
 
3. In the public comments section, Lindberg said that there is a webinar available 
describing how emergency public infrastructure spending in Vermont will work. It 
takes place on May 18th, at 1 p.m. Harik reiterated that the PC needs to understand 
the details of the spending plan ("It would be irresponsible not to figure out if we 
qualify"), and suggested that Norwich state representatives should be sought out for 
help. 
 
4. The Operations report was discussed, Eaton said that the new water meters have 
been ordered and should arrive by the end of May, and mentioned that there were 13

be held on June 11th at the Norwich Inn, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. The public is welcome

wear a mask (which will be provided). The topics to be discussed are: 
-- NFD priorities 
-- Infrastructure spending, with Representative Jim Masland (10:30 a.m.) 
-- Potential merger of assets with Norwich (discussion with the town manager) 
-- The NFD asset management plan 
-- The planned audit of the NFD 
-- Land management and tax exemptions 
-- Updating the long-range plan document

including descriptions and documents, and making them available online as NFD 101.

would not be able to attend today's meeting.

meeting (June 11th at 9:00 a.m.), and Lindberg mentioned that both meetings must 
be warned.

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
July 13, 2021 
Present:  PC voting members:  Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft, Elliot Harik; Water Department:  
Sam Eaton, Mike Tebbetts, Mike Wells; Treasurer:  Cheryl Lindberg; Auditor:  Priscilla Vincent; 
Clerk:  Steve Allen; Norwich Land Management Committee:  Byron Haynes, David Hubbard 
The meeting was called to order at 3:34 p.m.  
1. The day's Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
2. The minutes from the June 7th meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as amended 
to correct details related to Executive Session. 
 
3. There were no public comments. 
 
4. The PC greeted the new Water Operator, Mike Wells. It was moved, seconded, and 
approved to bring Wells on as a full-time employee as of August 2nd. 
 
5. Two members of the Norwich Land Management Committee, Byron Haynes and David 
Hubbard, gave an overview of the committee's activities and answered questions: 
 
-- Two new mountain bike trails have been constructed at Parcel 5, as well as a new 
connection to the Brookmead property owned by the Upper Valley Land Trust, allowing 
snow grooming equipment to move between the two; the footbridge from Parcel 5 to 
Brown's Schoolhouse Road/Ballard Trail has been completed.  
-- The Ballard trail is used more often now; grants from the Norwich Women's Club have 
been used to maintain bridges and other infrastructure on the trail; they are considering a 
project that will re-route part of the schoolhouse road that is particularly difficult to navigate.  
-- The LMC made $5,800 from selling timber last year; they took down some Red Pines at 
Tucker Hill Road and Beaver Meadow, re-planting some White Pines in their place; the 
seedlings were purchased from the State of New Hampshire nature store, and are working 
on a plan to plant another 150 trees next year on a property in that area; the company 
responsible for logging suggests painting all of the boundaries, to eliminate accidental 
cutting across borders. 
-- Conservation easements were discussed, with Haynes noting that it seems like a good 
idea because no one wants building along the Ballard Trail. The local bodies that 
buy/collect/enforce conservation easements are the VT Housing and Conservation Board 
and the Upper Valley Land Trust. The town of Norwich owns the development rights now, 
but no property taxes are collected - the development rights cannot be held in perpetuity.  
Someone expressed concern about the Upper Valley Land Trust owning the easement, as 
perhaps they are overwhelmed by the property they already own and won't manage it well. 

Vincent pointed out that the owner of an easement will only enforce the terms of the 
agreement, not manage the property. 
Hubbard said that an easement agreement can be customized to include carve-outs of 
areas to remain without restrictions. He also mentioned that some of the discussions in the 
town about expanding affordable housing have included questions about using Parcel 5 in 
that plan. 
Haynes said that the Charles Brown Brook running through the Ballard Trail property is an 
important waterway and would be an attractive easement project. Harik suggested that this 
issue should be linked to discussions with the town of a potential merger of assets; he also 
asked whether potential carbon off-sets could be linked to an easement. 
Harik:  in general, if someone wanted to oversee your work, how would they do it? 
Hubbard:  the Norwich Finance Department has oversight and all relevant information. 
Harik:  is there an existing "forestry plan" in place, and is it something we can look at? 
Hubbard:  yes, including a soil survey, delineation of wetlands, etc. 
Lindberg:  who is signing the contracts for the work done? 
Hubbard:  The Norwich LMC. 
Lindberg:  I'm not sure that's appropriate, that a committee appointed by the town signs 
these. I think it should be elected officials, either from the town or the NFD. I also think we 
need to clear up a number of questions on potential easements, who owns them, etc. We 
may need to talk to a lawyer about it. 
 
6. Eaton gave the Operations Report, including a discussion of a new water connection for 
Dan & Whit's for fire sprinklers, which will bring in $1,000 of revenue; there was a discussion 
of how sprinklers are similar to fire hydrants. The Hazen Street and Cliff Street contract will 
be more than anticipated, at $13,700 vs $10,000; the paint for the reservoir will be $5,000, 
vs $2,000 that had been expected. It was moved, seconded, and approved to accept the 
Operations Report as presented and to approve the report's action items. 
 
7. Lindberg gave the Treasurer's Report, noting that the Grand List of the NFD has increased 
from 382 parcels last year to 385 parcels now, and has increased in value by $1.3 million; 
this may make it possible to keep the tax rate at the same level as last year's. It was moved, 
seconded, and approved to accept the Treasurer's Report as presented. 
 
8. Other issues were discussed. Goodrich noted that he had a conversation with the chief of 
the town Fire Department about the Cliff Street break caused by the pressure shock. They 
have agreed to pay the repair costs, as well as to notify the NFD when hydrants will be used 
in the future. The potential audit was also discussed. 
Goodrich:  is an audit mandatory? 
Lindberg:  no, but it's a good idea to do it every 10 years. It might be necessary for future 
financing. 
Goodrich:  if we don't strictly need it, is it worth $10,000? 

Lindberg:  $10,000 was a guess, it might be less. I think we should at least put out the RFP 
and see what we're talking about.  
Groft:  the town audits itself, and we have Priscilla Vincent as an auditor. 
Lindberg:  if a body receives funds from the government, which we might in the future, they 
often want an outside audit to see that the money is spent well. Vincent does a good job 
with her audit, but an outside auditor would take additional steps.  
It was agreed that per Harik's suggestion elements from the long-term Priority List should be 
considered at each NFD meeting. Conducting meetings via Zoom may or may not continue, 
now that Covid restrictions have been lifted.   
 
9. The date for the next PC meeting was set for August 27th at 8:30 a.m., with the place to be 
determined.  The discussion will focus on operations, audits, financials from June, and the 
Priority List.  
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 5:02 p.m. 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
August 27, 2021 
Present:  Prudential Committee members: Michael Goodrich, Alicia Groft; Treasurer: Cheryl 
Lindberg; Clerk: Steve Allen; Water Department: Sam Eaton, Michael Tebbetts; Auditor:  
Priscilla Vincent. 
The meeting was called to order at 8:33 a.m.  
1. The Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented; 
 
2. The minutes from the July 13th meeting were moved, seconded, and approved as 
presented. 
 
3. Goodrich said in the public comments that, due to technical/pipe reasons, the proposed 
geothermal project with the town will not work. Allen announced that for personal reasons he 
will resign as Clerk. Groft asked who will replace him, and Goodrich said that he is looking at 
several options. 
 
4. The Treasurer's report was discussed, including that tax bills have been sent and that the 
hydrant rental fee to the town will be soon; in addition, the funds from the town to pay for the 
water main break on Cliff Street by the Fire Department have been received. It was moved, 
seconded, and approved to accept the Treasurer's report as presented. 
 
5. The Operations report was discussed, including engineering aspects of the I-91 pipe 
replacement project and boring techniques that might be used. Goodrich mentioned that he 
and Tebbetts discussed Parcel 5 with the town Affordable Housing Committee - he felt that 
it was a productive discussion and that the committee went away with the understanding 
that there are no appropriate building sites on Parcel 5. Lindberg asked where the 35 new 
meters have been installed, whether there have been any lessons learned, and whether the 
meters had yet been read by the new system. Eaton responded that the homes most difficult 
to access were the first recipients; Tebbetts noted that they are waiting on a package that 
will link water data to NEMRC - this should not be a problem as NEMRC has been dealing 
with this kind of data for decades, and the cost should only be about $350. Groft asked 
whether the cost of materials is up because of Covid. Eaton noted that costs are up 30% for 
many things, plus there are now time delays. Lindberg said that it may be unusually easy for 
municipalities to borrow right now. Groft summarized as "costs could go down so we could 
wait, but we don't know if interest rates will go up." - no one disagreed. Lindberg mentioned 
that the town had received $300,000 in grants and asked whether we can remain on the 
radar for some of that. Goodrich replied that town manager Durfee said in July that this was 
unlikely. It was moved, seconded, and approved to accept the Operations report as 
presented. 
 
6. There was a brief discussion of the Priority List. 
 

7. There was a discussion of the budget. Eaton said that the most important question is how to 
fund the Hazen Street and Cliff Street projects; he noted that it is hard to split them apart 
because of the physical layout. Groft said that there is $300,000 in the Reserve Fund, and 
that at least part of that could be used to fund the projects. She also suggested that finishing 
the RFP for an audit and putting it out might remove one obstacle to potential grants.  
 
8. There was a discussion of the potential merger with the town. Goodrich and Groft discussed 
what Roger Arnold has looked at on this question and what his opinion might be. Lindberg 
noted that the town government is not in the best place right now to evaluate complex 
issues, and that Roger is also time-constrained for the same reason [because he works for 
the town]. Goodrich countered that it may be the best time to make the NFD case clear.  
 
9. The date for the next PC meeting was set for September 14th at 8:00 a.m., with the place to 
be determined.  The discussion will focus on the Priority List, the budget, the potential 
merger with the town, and the RFP for an audit. 
 
The PC adjourned the meeting at 9:22 a.m. 
Steve Allen, Clerk

NORWICH FIRE DISTRICT 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE MINUTES 
September 14, 2021 
Present 
Prudential Committee (PC) Members: Michael Goodrich (Chair) and Alicia Groft 
Treasurer: Cheryl Lindberg 
Clerk: Daniel Officer 
Water Department: Sam Eaton 
Auditor: Priscilla Vincent 
Public: Linda Cook 
Regrets 
PC Member: Elliot Harik 
 
1. Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 8:08am. 
2. Approval of Agenda: The Agenda was moved, seconded, and approved as presented. 
3. Appointment of New Clerk: Daniel Officer was recruited to replace Steve Allen as Fire District Clerk 
following Allen's resignation from the role. A motion to appoint Officer to the Clerk position was made, 
seconded and voted unanimous.  
4. Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes: The minutes from the August 27th meeting were reviewed and select 
changes were proposed. A motion was made to approve the minutes, as amended, seconded and voted 
unanimous. 
5. Public Comment: Vincent thanked Officer for agreeing to fill the Clerk role. 
6. Treasurer's Report: Lindberg noted a majority of the Fire District tax payments has been received. Another 
tax reminder will be posted on the ListServ before the payment deadline of September 30. Lindberg also 
noted the August financials are coming together. A motion was made to approve the Treasurer's Report, 
seconded and voted unanimous. 
7. Operations Report: There was no Operations Report.  
8. Review of RFP for Audit: The Request for Proposal (RFP) for an Audit of the Fire District's financials was 
reviewed and select modifications were proposed. There was general discussion about the desire to issue 
the RFP soon to stay on schedule with the bid solicitation process. There was further discussion about how 
the RFP will be distributed to potential auditors. A motion was made to approve the RFP, as amended, 
seconded and voted unanimous.    
9. Discussion of Priority List: There was general discussion about the Priority List, including identifying the 
five core Priority List items as (a) Fire District Audit, (b) Asset Management Plan, (c) Fire District 2022 
Budget, (d) potential Fire District Merger with Town, and (e) general Fire District Financial Planning/Policies. 
The Priority List conversation covered the overlapping agenda topics relating to the Budget Discussion and 
Merger Discussion. The PC discussed specific actions for these items. For the Budget, Lindberg will provide 
a copy of the current 2021 budget and the PC will review and start to prep the 2022 budget. For the Merger, 
the PC will work on a document for the Selectboard then arrange a discussion with the Selectboard. 
10. Determination of Next Meeting: The date and time for the next PC meeting was set for October 5th at 8am. 
After the meeting, the PC discovered a scheduling conflict on the 5th and decided to move the date and time 
for the next meeting to October 12th at 8am. Accordingly, the next meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 
12th at 8am at place to be determined. 
11. Adjournment of Meeting: A motion was made to adjourn the meeting, seconded and voted unanimous at 
9:04am. 
 
Daniel Officer, Clerk

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * April 16, 2026 *  
Page 1 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE  -  SHERBURNE FIRE DISTRICT #1 
 
SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT OFFICE BUILDING & ZOOM  
 
Minutes of April 16, 2026 
 
 
Present: 
Christopher Karr  
 
 
 
Start:  4:00 p.m. 
Domenic Chiarella 
 
 
 
End:    4:35 p.m.  
 
      
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dave Lewis, District Manager 
 
 
 
John Gates, Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Bill Longley, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Brett Vereecke, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER - Chris called the meeting to order at 4:00 p.m. 
 
2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF JANUARY 22, 2026 MEETING - 
Domenic moved that the Prudential Committee Minutes of January 22, 2026 
be approved as written. Chris seconded. All in favor. 
 
3. CITIZEN'S INPUT - None 
 
4. PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE INPUT - None 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE - None   
  
6. DISTRICT MANAGER'S REPORT - 
   
a. JANUARY 1 - APRIL 1, 2026 FINANCIAL REPORT - Dave had previously 
sent the January 1 - April 1, 2026 financial report to the 
Prudential Committee.  This is the ¼ of the year report and Dave 
stated that everything looks normal for this early.  Domenic made 
the motion to approve the January 1 - April 1, 2026 financial 
report. Chris seconded. All in favor. 
 
b. UPDATE ON ERU INQUIRES & CONNECTIONS - Dave reported that Joshua 
Lanni has purchased 1.00 ERU for his lot on Priscilla Lane. Dave 
went over the other inquiries currently pending with nothing new 
to report.  The 2026 O&M Assessment bills were sent out this week.  
 
c. STATUS OF EFFLUENT PUMPS, MOTORS & CONTROLS - Dave and John outlined 
the status of this project.  The two pumps (#2 & #3) and motors 
are on order for $102,320. Laramie Water Resources has pulled the 
failed Pump #2 and evaluated it for $10,884.  The Laramie estimate 
just received to remove Pump #3, install two new pumps and motors, 
as well as the surge relief valves etc is $115,657 which will 
change somewhat but hopefully not by much.  That leaves the electric 
controls to purchase and install which we don't have a firm price 
yet.  We should be able to do the entire project for about the 
$250K which was estimated. While we don't have to change the Pump 
#3 motor to explosion proof now we do have to agree to do this in 
the future. Dave suggested adding it to the RBC replacement 
project. 

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * April 16, 2026 *  
Page 2 
 
 
d. STATUS OF FINAL DESIGN & STATE FUNDING - Dave reported that we were 
not included in the Vermont ANR 2026 Priority List for construction 
funding and in fact we were near the bottom of the list: third from 
the bottom.  The funding cut-off was at 66 priority points while 
we had only 24 points.  Perhaps when we get our Step II Final 
Design completed and approved and have a successful bond vote so 
we are ready to build, our points will be higher, and we'll have a 
better chance to get funded. Hopefully DG will finish the design 
this year and provide an accurate cost estimate so we can schedule 
a bond vote for late 2026 or early 2027.  
 
 
7. TREATMENT PLANT OPERATOR'S REPORT -  
John sent the Operator's Report to Dave and the Prudential Committee. A 
problem with the sludge pump has been repaired.  The potable well pump 
failed and it has been replaced under warranty.  New wire to the new 
pump was installed.  There was a power outage on March 7 and again today. 
Odor issues seem better as there have been no new complaints. 
The effluent pump project was discussed earlier.  The fence between the 
plant and the Pickle Barrel has broken and will need to be taken down.  
Originally it had three sides but two had been removed previously. Chris 
noted that a lot of people walk out there so it might be a good idea to 
replace the fence.  Dave suggested looking into a shorter fiberglass 
fence which could be removed for the RBC work and then reinstalled.  It 
would still provide a visual barrier. 
 
 
8. SET NEXT MEETING - The next Prudential Committee meeting will be Thursday 
June 25, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. at the Sewage Treatment Plant Office Building 
& Zoom. 
 
 
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 4:35 p.m.

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * August 13, 2026 *  
Page 1 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE  -  SHERBURNE FIRE DISTRICT #1 
 
SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT OFFICE BUILDING & ZOOM  
 
Minutes of August 13, 2026 
 
 
Present: 
Christopher Karr  
 
 
 
Start:  4:04 p.m. 
Domenic Chiarella 
 
 
 
End:    4:55 p.m.  
Ken Peters 
 
      
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dave Lewis, District Manager 
 
 
 
John Gates, Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Bill Longley, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Brett Vereecke, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER - Chris called the meeting to order at 4:04 p.m. 
 
2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF JUNE 30, 2026 MEETING - 
Domenic moved that the Prudential Committee Minutes of June 30, 2026 be 
approved as written. Chris seconded. All in favor.  Ken was not present 
for this vote.   
 
3. CITIZEN'S INPUT - None 
 
4. PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE INPUT - Domenic reported that he will have his 
attorney draft up a warranty deed to the Fire District for the Dean Hill 
Road sewer line.   He noted that it has 3 connections on it at present 
and has capacity for a total of 7.  Discussion was held on the difference 
between this line and the Mikula line from his house to a SFD manhole. 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE - None   
  
6. DISTRICT MANAGER'S REPORT - 
   
a. JANUARY 1 - AUGUST 1, 2026 FINANCIAL REPORT - Dave had previously 
sent both the January 1 - July 1 and August 1, 2026 financial 
reports to the Prudential Committee.   
Dave stated that everything looks good at this point with 
Delinquent Assessment collections being very good. The status of 
individual accounts was discussed.  The State of Vermont has been 
paid for the outfall relocation work on Route 4.  Dave has submitted 
a reimbursement request to ANR for about $15,500 of Dufresne Group 
invoices for 2026.   
Domenic made the motion to approve the January 1 - August 1, 2026 
financial report. Chris seconded. All in favor.  Ken was not present 
for this vote. 
 
b. UPDATE ON ERU INQUIRES & CONNECTIONS - Dave mentioned that the West 
Hill Lot #60 project seems to be moving along which would subdivide 
into 6 lots.  
 
 

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * August 13, 2026 *  
Page 2 
 
c. STATUS OF EFFLUENT PUMPS, MOTORS & CONTROLS - John outlined the 
status of this project under his Operator's Report.  
  
d. STATUS OF FINAL DESIGN & STATE FUNDING - Dave reported on the 
reimbursement request in his report and John discussed the Final 
Design status in his report.    
 
7. TREATMENT PLANT OPERATOR'S REPORT -  
John sent the Operator's Report to Dave and the Prudential Committee. 
The new Effluent Pump #2 was installed a few weeks ago.  Some parts are 
still not here to finish that work, which will hopefully be done by mid-
September.  Don Martin has been given the go ahead to start the electrical 
work which will cost $79,104 including a $30K panel.  
Dufresne Group has completed the design of the RBC replacement project.  
They have a construction cost estimate of $2,245,000 and an estimated 
Total project cost of $2,930,500.  There hasn't been any discussion about 
breaking the project into two phases yet.  Discussion was held on funding 
the project without ANR Vermont Bond Bank money or to move ahead with 
the project using all our own funds which would likely result in at least 
double the interest rate from the ANR subsidized 2% loan funds.  
Once the Final Design has been approved by the State, we should consider 
a bond vote in 2027 to be ready to use unexpended ANR Bond Funds or move 
ahead on our own. 
John submitted the Fire Safety Permit application to the State which 
cost $1,578.91.   
John reported that he purchased a laptop computer to replace our obsolete 
desktop.    Lowell Fence will be installing the fence this fall, hopefully 
before winter hits.    
John reached out to Casella, Markowski and Mosher on the manhole work 
but they either didn't respond or can't do the work. John spoke again 
with Charlie Bowen who can do the manhole work for about $2,000- $3,000 
for the two worst ones.   
 
8. SET NEXT MEETING - The next Prudential Committee meeting will be Thursday 
October 15, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. at the Sewage Treatment Plant Office 
Building & Zoom. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 4:55 p.m.

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * January 22, 2026 *  
Page 1 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE  -  SHERBURNE FIRE DISTRICT #1 
 
SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT OFFICE BUILDING & ZOOM  
 
Minutes of January 22, 2026 
 
 
Present: 
Christopher Karr  
 
 
 
Start:  4:04 p.m. 
Domenic Chiarella 
 
 
 
End:    5:57 p.m.  
Ken Peters  
 
      
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dave Lewis, District Manager 
 
 
 
John Gates, Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Bill Longley, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Brett Vereecke, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER - Chris called the meeting to order at 4:04 p.m. 
 
2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF DECEMBER 18, 2025 MEETING - 
Domenic moved that the Prudential Committee Minutes of December 18, 2025 
be approved as written. Ken seconded. All in favor. 
 
3. CITIZEN'S INPUT - None 
 
4. PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE INPUT - Chris reported that BGR who own a house off 
Dean Hill Road behind the Pickle Barrel is interested in connecting to 
the Fire District. 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE - None   
  
6. DISTRICT MANAGER'S REPORT - 
   
a. JANUARY 1 - DECEMBER 31, 2025 FINANCIAL REPORT - Dave had previously 
sent the January 1 - December 31, 2025 financial report to the 
Prudential Committee.  This is the year-end report.  Dave noted 
that not counting the Miscellaneous to be Reimbursed line item, 
total expenditures were over budget by $14,000 and this was due to 
the Construction Projects category being $16,000 over the budget. 
Revenues were good with strong delinquent collections and as 
expected current O&M assessment collections.  Domenic made the 
motion to approve the January 1 - December 31, 2025 year-end 
financial report. Ken seconded. All in favor. 
 
b. UPDATE ON ERU INQUIRES & CONNECTIONS - Dave reported that there 
have been a number on inquiries over the past few months that seem 
to still be in limbo with nothing new to report, other than the 
new one Chris mentioned today.  The Rivershed sale is apparently 
on hold. Previous inquiries about a Mountain View Drive lot, 
Priscilla Lane & Dean Hill Road lots, Butler Road & McClellan Drive 
houses, Killington Mountain School, Durkee property and others are 
still in the works.  
 
c. STATUS OF FINAL DESIGN & STATE REIMBURSEMENTS - Dave reported that 
we haven't received the submitted $31,481.00 reimbursement yet 

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * January 22, 2026 *  
Page 2 
 
although it has been approved by the State. John reported that the 
90% Final Design, due December 15th , still hasn't been received 
and could be changed if we do something now with the effluent 
pumping system instead of waiting until 2027/2028.  
 
d. AUTHORIZE SIGNATURES ON MARCH 2, 2026 ANNUAL MEETING WARNING - Dave 
noted that the 2026 Annual Meeting Warning must be officially 
signed during this time frame.  Domenic made the motion to authorize 
the Prudential Committee signatures on the March 2, 2026 Annual 
Meeting Warning dated today. Ken seconded.  All in favor.   
 
e. DISCUSS EFFLUENT PUMP #2 - Dave and John provided updates on the 
quickly changing issues with the effluent pumps, motors, controls, 
wiring and Parco valves.  The #2 pump is down and now the #1 back-
up pump has developed a problem, which turned out to be a limit 
switch failure and a bad relay.  The bond project design includes 
the replacement of Pump #2, Pump #3, motors for both and a new 
valve system to replace all the existing Parco valves.  New wiring 
and a new control panel for all three pumps, motors and valves are 
also planned. Considering the new problems, discussion was held on 
pulling the entire effluent pump system components out of the bond 
vote and doing that portion now, paying for it out of the Capital 
Fund. The last estimate we received from Dufresne Group was that 
this work would cost about $250,000 but it is unclear what exactly 
that consisted of and whether it is a realistic estimate now. The 
lead time on new pumps is 20 weeks which could stretch out to 6 
months. Furthermore, John has learned from Phil Laramie of Laramie 
Water Resources of an alternative to the ball valve replacement 
suggested by DG which may need to be explosion proof.  The Laramie 
suggestion is a mechanical check valve air release system and John 
has requested DG to investigate this alternative.  The Prudential 
Committee agreed to have Dave and John ask DG for a new estimate 
and description of the separated effluent pumping system so we can 
decide on moving forward with this work immediately. 
 
 
7. TREATMENT PLANT OPERATOR'S REPORT -  
John sent the Operator's Report to Dave and the Prudential Committee. 
The report mainly dealt with the effluent pumping system which was 
discussed at length as part of the item above. 
 
 
8. SET NEXT MEETING - The next Prudential Committee meeting will be Thursday 
April 16, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. at the Sewage Treatment Plant Office Building 
& Zoom. 
 
ANNUAL FIRE DISTRICT MEETING - MONDAY MARCH 2, 2026 AT 4:00 P.M. AT 
SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT OFFICE BUILDING & ZOOM. 
 
 
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 5:57 p.m.

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * June 30, 2026 *  
Page 1 
 
 
 
 
PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE  -  SHERBURNE FIRE DISTRICT #1 
 
SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT OFFICE BUILDING & ZOOM  
 
Minutes of June 30, 2026 
 
 
Present: 
Christopher Karr  
 
 
 
Start:  4:10 p.m. 
Domenic Chiarella 
 
 
 
End:    5:50 p.m.  
Ken Peters 
 
      
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dave Lewis, District Manager 
 
 
 
John Gates, Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Bill Longley, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
Brett Vereecke, Assistant Treatment Plant Operator 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER - Chris called the meeting to order at 4:10 p.m. 
 
2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF APRIL 16, 2026 MEETING - 
Domenic moved that the Prudential Committee Minutes of April 16, 2026 
be approved as written. Ken seconded. All in favor. 
 
3. CITIZEN'S INPUT - None 
 
4. PRUDENTIAL COMMITTEE INPUT - Domenic reported that he has listed his 
house for sale and plans to move out of the Fire District at some point 
in the future which would cause his seat to become vacant.  The 
Prudential Committee felt that the March 2027 Annual Meeting would be 
the appropriate time to fill the seat.  Stephanie's District Clerk and 
Treasurer positions would also have to be filled at the same time. 
 
Domenic brought up his desire to transfer the Dean Hill Road 2-inch 
force sewer line to the Fire District.  It was built by Red Glaze about 
20 years ago and has worked well but needs a new owner.  It is owned by 
an LLC and could be easily transferred.  Domenic will put together some 
documentation and a proposal for the Prudential Committee to review. 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE - None   
  
6. DISTRICT MANAGER'S REPORT - 
   
a. JANUARY 1 - JUNE 1, 2026 FINANCIAL REPORT - Dave had previously 
sent the January 1 - June 1, 2026 financial report to the Prudential 
Committee.  This is the 1/3 of the year report and Dave stated that 
everything looks good at this point.  A lot of discussion ensued 
regarding the General Fund, Capital Fund and the Additional ERU 
Sales Special Fund Balances.  The General Fund expected year-end 
balance is as low as we will want it to be as the current O&M 
assessments along with penalty & interest earnings will still be a 
little under the expected expenditures, which would mean next 
year's O&M rates will need to be increased again.   
The Capital Fund will be reduced by the $110,000 we owe the State 
of Vermont for the Route 4 sewer relocation work done a couple of 
years ago due to the new State Culvert plus the ongoing Effluent 

SFD # 1 * Prudential Committee Meeting Minutes * June 30, 2026 *  
Page 2 
 
Pumps and Motors project expenditures, which looks like will be at 
least $300,000.  This will reduce our year-end Capital Fund balance 
to under $140,000.  We still will have this amount plus over 
$300,000 in the Special ERU Sales Fund available for General Fund 
support and future Capital projects such as the RBC Replacement 
project which DG is currently finishing up the design.  
Domenic made the motion to approve the January 1 -June 1, 2026 
financial report. Ken seconded. All in favor. 
 
b. UPDATE ON ERU INQUIRES & CONNECTIONS - Dave reported that there 
hasn't been anything new to report since the last meeting.  
 
c. STATUS OF EFFLUENT PUMPS, MOTORS & CONTROLS - Dave and John outlined 
the status of this project.  The two pumps (#2 & #3) and motors 
have arrived and are ready to install once the electrical design, 
quote and delivery is accomplished. Laramie Water Resources will 
be ready to begin partial installation the week of July 27th.  The 
anticipated cost for this project is discussed above. 
 
d. STATUS OF FINAL DESIGN & STATE FUNDING - Dave reported that since 
we will likely not get a 2% Vermont Bond Bank loan due to our low 
priority points we need to plan how to replace the RBC's and gates 
with our own funds.  The DG design should be completed this year, 
which should give us a better idea of the expected costs so we 
could schedule a bond vote for early in 2027.  If we are still not 
high enough on the priority list, then we might consider breaking 
up the RBC replacements into two projects split into two or three 
years to stretch out our own funds and reduce and delay the new 
bond repayment closer to when our current bond is paid off.    
 
7. TREATMENT PLANT OPERATOR'S REPORT -  
John sent the Operator's Report to Dave and the Prudential Committee. 
As reported last time, the Fire District had to pay for the new wire to 
the warranty replaced water well pump, which was $2,532.  John outlined 
the options for replacing the fence between the plant and the Pickle 
Barrel parking lot.  It was decided to go with the least expensive and 
shortest chain-link fence for $3,600.  It will be 6 feet high, have 
sleeved posts to allow removal for access from the parking lot and will 
have privacy slots.  The fence could be extended if it was desired to 
do so in the future. 
John had some camera work done and they found 3 leaks and some manholes 
in disrepair.  John spoke with Charlie Bowen about doing the manhole 
work.  It was suggested to inquire if Charlie is capable of doing this 
and perhaps contact Mosher, Belden and/or Casella if he can't.  The leaks 
should be able to be fixed by a cured in place pipe sleeve system that 
we used last year. 
John reported that the City of Rutland sludge disposal dumping fee will 
be increasing from 14 Cents/gallon to 19 Cents which will result in an 
estimated $7,700 yearly increase in our sludge disposal costs. 
 
8. SET NEXT MEETING - The next Prudential Committee meeting will be Thursday 
August 13, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. at the Sewage Treatment Plant Office 
Building & Zoom. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 5:50 p.m.

This report is a snapshot of the quality of the water that we provided in 2025. Included are the details about where your water 
comes from, what it contains, and how it compares to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and state standards. We are 
committed to providing you with information because informed customers are our best allies. This report is designed to inform 
you about the quality water and services we deliver to you every day. To learn more, please attend any of our regularly

The person who can answer questions about this report is: Chris Lavoy

Please share this information with all the other people who drink this water, especially those who may not have received this 
notice directly (for example, people in apartments, nursing homes, schools, and businesses). You can do this by posting this 
notice in a public place and distributing copies by hand or mail. 
As required by the Lead and Copper Rule Revision, we have prepared a service line inventory. The purpose of the inventory 
was to determine if any of our service lines contain lead, galvanized pipe requiring removal, or unknown materials. Please 
contact us if you would like access to this inventory.

The State of Vermont Water Supply Rule requires Public Community Water Systems to develop a Source Protection Plan. This 
plan delineates a source protection area for our system and identifies potential and actual sources of contamination. Please 
contact us if you are interested in reviewing the plan. 
Drinking Water Contaminants 
The sources of drinking water (both tap water and bottled water) include surface water (streams, lakes) and ground water (wells, 
springs). As water travels over the land's surface or through the ground, it dissolves naturally-occurring minerals. It also picks 
up substances resulting from the presence of animals and human activity. Some "contaminants" may be harmful. Others, such 
as iron and sulfur, are not harmful. Public water systems treat water to remove contaminants, if any are present. 
In order to ensure that your water is safe to drink, we test it regularly according to regulations established by the U.S. 
Environmental Protection Agency and the State of Vermont. These regulations limit the amount of various contaminants: 
Microbial contaminants, such as viruses and bacteria, which may come from sewage treatment plants, septic systems, 
agricultural livestock operations and wildlife 
Inorganic contaminants, such as salts and metals, which can be naturally-occurring or result from urban storm water runoff, 
industrial or domestic wastewater discharges, oil and gas production, mining or farming. 
Pesticides and herbicides, may come from a variety of sources such as storm water run-off, agriculture, and residential users. 
Radioactive contaminants, which can be naturally occurring or the result of mining activity. 

Organic contaminants, including synthetic and volatile organic chemicals, which are by-products of industrial processes and 
petroleum production, and also come from gas stations, urban storm water run-off, and septic systems. 
Water Quality Data 
The table below lists all the drinking water contaminants that we detected during the past year. It also includes the date and 
results of any contaminants that we detected within the past five years if tested less than once a year. The presence of these 
contaminants in the water does not necessarily show that the water poses a health risk. 
Terms and abbreviations - In this table you may find terms you might not be familiar with. To help you better understand 
these terms we have provided the following definitions: 
Action Level (AL): The concentration of a contaminant which, if exceeded, triggers treatment or other requirements which a 
water system must follow. 
Contaminant: Any physical, chemical, biological, or radiological substance or matter in water. 
Corrosion Control Efforts: Treatment (including pH adjustment, alkalinity adjustment, or corrosion inhibitor addition) or 
other efforts contributing to the control of the corrosivity of water, e.g., monitoring to assess the corrosivity of water. 
Herbicide: Any chemical(s) used to control undesirable vegetation. 
Level 1 Assessment: A level 1 Assessment is a study of the water system to identify potential problems and determine (if 
possible) why total coliform bacteria have been found in our water system. 
Level 2 Assessment: A Level 2 Assessment is a very detailed study of the water system to identify potential problems and 
determine (if possible) why an E. coli MCL violation has occurred and/or why total coliform bacteria have been found in our 
water system on multiple occasions. 
Locational Running Annual Average (LRAA): The average of sample analytical results for samples taken at a particular 
monitoring location during four consecutive calendar quarters. 
Maximum Contamination Level (MCL): The "Maximum Allowed" MCL is the highest level of a contaminant that is allowed 
in drinking water. MCL's are set as close to the MCLG's as feasible using the best available treatment technology. 
Maximum Contamination Level Goal (MCLG): The "Goal" is the level of a contaminant in drinking water below which 
there is no known or expected risk to human health. MCLG's allow for a margin of safety. 
Maximum Residual Disinfectant Level (MRDL): The highest level of a disinfectant allowed in drinking water. Addition a 
disinfectant may help control microbial contaminants. 
Maximum Residual Disinfectant Level Goal (MRDLG): The level of a drinking water disinfectant below which there is no 
known or expected risk to health. MRDLGs do not reflect the benefits of disinfectants in controlling microbial contaminants. 
Method Reporting Limit: The lowest concentration of a chemical in a sample that a laboratory can reliably detect. 
Nephelometric Turbidity Unit (NTU): NTU is a measure of the clarity of water. Turbidity in excess of 5 NTU is just 
noticeable to the average person. 
Parts per million (ppm) or Milligrams per liter (mg/l): (one penny in ten thousand dollars) 
Parts per billion (ppb) or Micrograms per liter (µg/l): (one penny in ten million dollars) 
Parts per trillion (ppt) or Nanograms per liter (ng/l): (one penny in ten billion dollars) 
Pesticide: Generally, any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any 
pest. 
Picocuries per liter (pCi/L): a measure of radioactivity in water 
Running Annual Average (RAA): The average of 4 consecutive quarters (when on quarterly monitoring); values in table 
represent the highest RAA for the year. 
Treatment Technique (TT): A required process intended to reduce the level of a contaminant in drinking water. 
90th Percentile: Ninety percent of the samples are below the action level. (Nine of ten sites sampled were at or below this 
level). 
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS): PFAS are a group of human-made chemicals that have been in use since the 
1940s. PFAS have been found in a wide variety of consumer products and as an ingredient in firefighting foam. PFAS 
manufacturing and processing facilities, airports, and military installations are some of the contributors of PFAS releases into 
the air, soil and water. Vermont currently regulates 5 PFAS and this list includes: 
     Perfluorononanoic Acid (PFNA) 
     Perfluorooctanoic Acid (PFOA) 
     Perfluorooctane Sulfonic Acid (PFOS) 
     Perfluoroheptanoic Acid (PFHpA)

Health Information Regarding Drinking Water 
Some people may be more vulnerable to contaminants in drinking water than the general population. Immuno-compromised 
persons such as persons with cancer undergoing chemotherapy, persons who have undergone organ transplants, people with 
HIV/AIDS or other immune system disorders, some elderly, and infants, can be particularly at risk from infections. These 
people should seek advice about drinking water from their health care providers. EPA/CDC guidelines on appropriate means to 
lessen the risk of infection by cryptosporidium and other microbiological contaminants are available from EPA's Safe Drinking 
Water Hotline (1-800-426-4791). 
Drinking water, including bottled water, may reasonably be expected to contain at least small amounts of some contaminants. 
The presence of contaminants does not necessarily indicate that the water poses a health risk. More information about 
contaminants and potential health effects can be obtained by calling the Environmental Protection Agency's Safe Drinking 
Water Hotline (800-426-4791). 
Lead can cause serious health problems, especially for pregnant women and young children. Lead in drinking water is primarily 
from materials and components associated with service lines and home plumbing. WILMINGTON WATER DIST is 
responsible for providing high quality drinking water and removing lead pipes, but cannot control the variety of materials used 
in plumbing components in your home. You share the responsibility for protecting yourself and your family from the lead in 
your home plumbing. You can take responsibility by identifying and removing lead materials within your home plumbing and 
taking steps to reduce your family's risk. Before drinking tap water, flush your pipes for several minutes by running your tap, 
taking a shower, doing laundry or a load of dishes. You can also use a filter certified by an American National Standards 
Institute accredited certifier to reduce lead in drinking water. If you are concerned about lead in your water and you wish to 
have your water tested, contact WILMINGTON WATER DIST. Information on lead in drinking water, testing methods, and 
steps you can take to minimize exposure is available at https://www.epa.gov/safewater/lead.
